title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖癸卯秋楚當大比士監
察御史桂榮奉
命按治寔維監臨申嚴胥飭凡簾
內外百執事咸愼簡充之先
是前巡按御史史褒善稽典
肇事馳幣聘席珍等役校藝
===
至是咸集乃以席珍暨教諭
黃國奎考試教授林啓金白
沈文冕學正歐陽瑜教諭鄭
廷焯楊世瑞張堯弼潘愼學
分試而提調以屬左布政使
陳則清右參議陳塏監試以
屬副使張承恩僉事柯喬規
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖癸卯秋，楚當大比士。監察御史桂榮奉命按治，寔維監臨，申嚴胥飭。凡簾內外百執事，咸愼簡充之。先是，前巡按御史史褒善稽典肇事，馳幣聘席珍等役校藝。至是咸集，乃以席珍暨教諭黃國奎考試，教授林啓、金白、沈文冕，學正歐陽瑜，教諭鄭廷焯、楊世瑞、張堯弼、潘愼學分試。而提調以屬左布政使陳則清、右參議陳塏，監試以屬副使張承恩、僉事柯喬。規
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In autumn of the guimao year of Jiajing (1543), Chu was due to hold its triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Gui Rong, commanded to conduct an inspection of the region, served as Supervising Official. He reiterated strict requirements and enjoined discipline upon all. All personnel serving inside and outside the examination curtain were carefully selected for their duties. Previously, the former Regional Inspector, Shi Baoshan, had consulted the established regulations and initiated preparations, dispatching ceremonial gifts to invite Xi Zhen and others to evaluate the candidates’ compositions. By this time they had all assembled. Xi Zhen and County School Instructor Huang Guokui were appointed Examiners. Professors Lin Qi, Jin Bai, and Shen Wenmian; Departmental School Instructor Ouyang Yu; and County School Instructors Zheng Tingzhuo, Yang Shirui, Zhang Yaobi, and Pan Shenxue served as Associate Examiners. The duties of Proctor were entrusted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Zeqing and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Chen Kai. Supervision of the examination was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Cheng’en and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Ke Qiao. Their planning…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
畫維允罔弗寅恭期得眞賢
上翊
聖治維時尚書樊繼祖都御史潘
鑑以督木萬鏜以處夷先後
至振雅覿文所至講藝敦獎
逢掖都御史巡撫先陸杰今
車純保釐化誨人有寧宇士
===
咸思奮撫治鄖陽先喻茂堅
張岳今王守提督南贛先李
顯今虞守愚並崇軌率物章
志貞敎總兵豐城侯李熈雅
尚儒術守備太監傅霖郎中
王之臣員外郎沙稷主事郭
乾向宗哲陸愚樂觀鉅典右
punctuated:
畫維允，罔弗寅恭，期得眞賢，上翊聖治。

維時，尚書樊繼祖、都御史潘鑑以督木，萬鏜以處夷，先後至。振雅覿文，所至講藝，敦獎逢掖。都御史巡撫，先陸杰，今車純，保釐化誨，人有寧宇，士咸思奮。撫治鄖陽，先喻茂堅、張岳，今王守；提督南贛，先李顯，今虞守愚，並崇軌率物，章志貞敎。總兵豐城侯李熈，雅尚儒術。守備太監傅霖、郎中王之臣、員外郎沙稷、主事郭乾、向宗哲、陸愚，樂觀鉅典。右
translation_en:
…the arrangements were appropriate, and all conducted themselves with reverent care, hoping to select truly worthy men to assist the sage governance of His Majesty.

At this time, Minister Fan Jizu and Censor-in-chief Pan Jian came to supervise timber procurement, and Wan Tang came to handle affairs concerning the non-Han peoples. They arrived in succession. They promoted refined learning and surveyed literary accomplishments; wherever they went, they discussed scholarly composition and earnestly encouraged the Confucian scholars. The grand coordinators, holding the title of Censor-in-chief—formerly Lu Jie and now Che Chun—maintained order and provided moral instruction, so that the people had peaceful homes and the scholars all aspired to exert themselves. Those charged with pacifying and administering Yunyang—formerly Yu Maojian and Zhang Yue, and now Wang Shou—and those serving as supreme commanders in southern Ganzhou—formerly Li Xian and now Yu Shouyu—all upheld exemplary standards and guided others, made their purposes manifest, and kept instruction correct. Regional Commander Li Xi, Marquis of Fengcheng, had long esteemed Confucian learning. The Grand Defender, Grand Eunuch Fu Lin; Bureau Director Wang Zhichen; Vice Director Sha Ji; and Secretaries Guo Qian, Xiang Zongzhe, and Lu Yu delighted in witnessing this great ceremony. The Right …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
參政鄭重及宦右參議方遠
宜魏良輔蔣芝秦鰲副使李
義壯盧紳王學孔金瓅項喬
僉事楊雷米榮李磐孫雲都
指揮芮恩劉遠則皆協賛分
理于外副使馬坤左參議潘
九齡先期入賀
===
萬壽若左布政使今陞都御史顧
遂經慮飭材及左參政今陞
按察使胡有恒右參政今陞
府丞端廷赦都指揮今陞參
將李經雖先後去楚亦皆與
有聞焉者也旣圍棘鎖院御
史榮廼矢心勵眾合提學副
punctuated:
參政鄭重、及宦，右參議方遠宜、魏良輔、蔣芝、秦鰲，副使李義壯、盧紳、王學孔、金瓅、項喬，僉事楊雷、米榮、李磐、孫雲，都指揮芮恩、劉遠，則皆協賛分理于外。副使馬坤、左參議潘九齡，先期入賀萬壽。若左布政使今陞都御史顧遂，經慮飭材，及左參政今陞按察使胡有恒、右參政今陞府丞端廷赦、都指揮今陞參將李經，雖先後去楚，亦皆與有聞焉者也。
旣圍棘鎖院，御史榮廼矢心勵眾，合提學副
translation_en:
…Administration Vice Commissioners Zheng Zhong and Ji Huan; Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Fang Yuanyi, Wei Liangfu, Jiang Zhi, and Qin Ao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Li Yizhuang, Lu Shen, Wang Xuekong, Jin Li, and Xiang Qiao; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yang Lei, Mi Rong, Li Pan, and Sun Yun; and Regional Military Commissioners Rui En and Liu Yuan all assisted and shared responsibility for affairs outside the examination compound. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ma Kun and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Pan Jiuling had gone to court beforehand to offer congratulations on the emperor’s birthday. As for Left Administration Commissioner Gu Sui, now promoted to Censor-in-Chief, who planned the arrangements and put resources in order [?], together with Left Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Youheng, now promoted to Surveillance Commissioner; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Duan Tingshe, now promoted to Prefectural Vice Prefect; and Regional Military Commissioner Li Jing, now promoted to Assistant Regional Commander: although they had left Chu at different times, all had participated in these affairs.
Once the thorn enclosure had been set up and the examination compound locked, Censor Rong pledged his resolve and exhorted everyone, joining with the Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
使先孫繼魯令應檟所選士
二千六百有奇而三試之遵
近
制拔其雋九十人錄其文二十一
篇登之
天府而席珍以職務猥序首簡竊
惟楚芊之裔肇系高陽祝融
===
之職世嗣火正本神明之胄
荆衡鉅鎮江漢上游紀在職
方羽毛齒革金錫箘簵竝充
王貢土衍物豐莫之尚也矧
厲山之鄉有炎帝之播殖焉
瀟湘之湄有重華之巡狩焉
九江大别有神禹之疏鑿焉
punctuated:
使先孫繼魯、令應檟所選士二千六百有奇，而三試之。遵近制，拔其雋九十人，錄其文二十一篇，登之天府。而席珍以職務，猥序首簡。
竊惟楚芊之裔，肇系高陽，祝融之職，世嗣火正，本神明之胄。荆衡鉅鎮，江漢上游，紀在職方；羽毛齒革、金錫箘簵，竝充王貢。土衍物豐，莫之尚也。矧厲山之鄉，有炎帝之播殖焉；瀟湘之湄，有重華之巡狩焉；九江大别，有神禹之疏鑿焉；
translation_en:
…the more than 2,600 candidates selected by the former Education Intendant Sun Jilu and the incumbent Ying Jia [?], and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the recent regulations, ninety outstanding candidates were selected, and twenty-one of their compositions were recorded for submission to the imperial repository. I, Xi Zhen, by virtue of my official duties, have presumptuously supplied a preface for the opening pages.
I humbly reflect that Chu descended from the Qian clan [?], tracing its lineage to Gaoyang. Its ancestors held the office of Zhurong, hereditarily succeeding as Director of Fire: theirs was a lineage of divine beings. The great mountains Jing and Heng and the upper reaches of the Jiang and Han are recorded in the account of the Director of the Regions. Feathers, hair, ivory, hides, gold, tin, and fine arrow bamboo all supplied royal tribute. No land surpassed it in breadth of fertile soil and abundance of products. Moreover, in the countryside of Lishan, the Flame Emperor sowed and cultivated; along the banks of the Xiao and Xiang, Chonghua made his inspection tours; and at the Nine Rivers and Dabie, divine Yu dredged waterways and cut channels…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
江沱汝漢有文王之教化焉
迨至鬻熊寔為文武師而三
墳五典八索九丘盡在於楚
楚固文獻上國也是故靈淑
之所鍾神聖之所格不萃于
物則萃于人不作於前則作
於後蓋垂千年而得靈均離
===
騷之篇肇開辭賦而宋大夫
賈太傅衍之江鄉又垂千年
而得元公營道之居默契道
體而南軒考亭講之嶽麓然
或忠而未醇或醇而未庸君
子有遺憾焉迨于
今日貞元始合精英交鬯我
punctuated: 江沱汝漢，有文王之教化焉。迨至鬻熊，寔為文武師，而三墳、五典、八索、九丘盡在於楚。楚固文獻上國也。是故靈淑之所鍾，神聖之所格，不萃于物，則萃于人；不作於前，則作於後。蓋垂千年而得靈均，《離騷》之篇肇開辭賦，而宋大夫、賈太傅衍之江鄉。又垂千年而得元公，營道之居默契道體，而南軒、考亭講之嶽麓。然或忠而未醇，或醇而未庸，君子有遺憾焉。迨于今日，貞元始合，精英交鬯，我
translation_en: …Along the Jiang, Tuo, Ru, and Han rivers, King Wen’s transforming instruction held sway. Later, Yuxiong indeed served as teacher to Kings Wen and Wu, and the Three Tombs, Five Canons, Eight Cords, and Nine Mounds were all preserved in Chu. Chu was assuredly a foremost land of written traditions and worthy men. Thus, where spiritual excellence gathers and the divine sages have reached, it manifests itself, if not in things, then in people; if not in earlier times, then in later ones. After nearly a thousand years came Lingjun [Qu Yuan], whose Encountering Sorrow inaugurated the tradition of lyric poetry and rhapsody; Grand Master Song [Song Yu] and Grand Tutor Jia [Jia Yi] extended that tradition in the river country. After nearly another thousand years came Duke Yuan [Zhou Dunyi], who, dwelling in Yingdao, attained a silent understanding of the substance of the Way; Nanxuan [Zhang Shi] and Kaoting [Zhu Xi] expounded it at Yuelu. Yet some were loyal without attaining purity, while others attained purity without putting it into practice, leaving gentlemen with cause for regret. Now, in our own day, completion and renewal have at last joined, and the finest essences flourish together. Our …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇上發潛
興邸出震
郢郊秉
元聖之資正
大寶之位荆楚之士固已睹
聖萬物之先矣禮樂明倫制盡涵
濡煦嫗二十二年于兹間者
===
升祔之舉
大狩之臨
敷告之播
典章之述
動爲世道
言爲世則士尤目覿心醉優柔
厭飫成人小子靡不底于造
punctuated: 皇上發潛興邸，出震郢郊，秉元聖之資，正大寶之位。荆楚之士固已睹聖萬物之先矣。禮樂明倫制盡涵濡煦嫗，二十二年于兹。間者，升祔之舉，大狩之臨，敷告之播，典章之述，動爲世道，言爲世則。士尤目覿心醉，優柔厭飫，成人小子靡不底于造
translation_en: …His Majesty emerged from seclusion at the residence of the Prince of Xing and came forth as sovereign from the outskirts of Ying. Endowed with the qualities of a supreme sage, he assumed his rightful place on the imperial throne. The scholars of Jing and Chu had thus already beheld the sage before all other beings. Through rites, music, the clarification of human relationships, and institutions [?], all have received his nurturing warmth for twenty-two years now. Recently came the elevation and enshrinement in the ancestral temple, his arrival on the great imperial hunt, the dissemination of proclamations, and the exposition of statutes and institutions. His actions provide a way for the age; his words provide its standards. The scholars, especially, have witnessed these things with their own eyes and been enraptured in their hearts, imbibing them at leisure and to the full. Among adults and youths alike, none has failed to attain…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
德頃用御史姚虞饒天民言
復增解額士益知
上意所嚮咸思奮庸仰煕
帝載故席珍等日夕校閱其言蜿
蜒磅礴而峭拔汪洋𨯳磕而
演迤斯山祇川若之委和也
其言雅麗而典飭端嚴而敷
===
===
腴斯
神謨
聖德之錫極也盖扣之有弗盡其
蘊取之有弗盡其才楚之士
于兹盛矣夫雲從風靡聲應
氣求類也矧數千餘禩地氣
人文濬哲而長發者乎世運
punctuated: 德。頃用御史姚虞、饒天民言，復增解額，士益知上意所嚮，咸思奮庸，仰煕帝載。故席珍等日夕校閱，其言蜿蜒磅礴而峭拔，汪洋𨯳磕而演迤，斯山祇川若之委和也；其言雅麗而典飭，端嚴而敷腴，斯神謨聖德之錫極也。盖扣之有弗盡其蘊，取之有弗盡其才，楚之士于兹盛矣。夫雲從風靡，聲應氣求，類也，矧數千餘禩地氣人文濬哲而長發者乎？世運
translation_en: …virtue. Recently, acting upon the recommendations of the Censors Yao Yu and Rao Tianmin, His Majesty again increased the quota for provincial graduates. The scholars understood all the more clearly the direction of the imperial will, and all aspired to exert themselves in service and help advance the Emperor’s undertakings. Thus Xizhen and the other examiners reviewed their writings day and night. Their language winds and unfolds, vast in scope yet soaring in force; it surges expansively with a resounding tumult [?], yet flows onward at ease. This is the harmonious influence bestowed by the spirits of the mountains and rivers. Their language is elegant and beautiful, yet ordered by classical standards; dignified and solemn, yet rich and full. This is the supreme standard bestowed through His Majesty’s divine counsels and sagely virtue. Indeed, questioning them cannot exhaust their depth, nor drawing upon them exhaust their talent. The scholars of Chu have now attained such flourishing excellence! Clouds follow and things bend before the wind; sounds respond to one another and kindred vital forces seek one another out: these are affinities of kind. How much more must this be so where, for several thousand years, the vital forces of the land and the cultural accomplishments of its people have fostered profound wisdom and enduring growth! The course of the age…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之會豈偶然哉抑王國之士
固思皇譽髦之流也四方耳
目于此乎繫故皇帝王霸性
命道德從而徵術焉乾符坤
輿民宜物類文經武緯從而
徵學焉財成左右彌綸叅賛
從而徵業焉然此皆性也非
===
由外鑠也反身而求萬物皆
備故靈淑之孕毓神聖之謨
烈忠醇之抒溁見吾性之中
焉見吾性之和焉推而致之
大本立達道行可以孚四方
之觀聽矣不然遺實而徇名
略近而騖遠周行之忽而旁
punctuated: 之會，豈偶然哉？抑王國之士，固思皇譽髦之流也。四方耳目于此乎繫，故皇帝王霸、性命道德，從而徵術焉；乾符坤輿、民宜物類、文經武緯，從而徵學焉；財成左右、彌綸叅賛，從而徵業焉。然此皆性也，非由外鑠也。反身而求，萬物皆備。故靈淑之孕毓、神聖之謨烈、忠醇之抒溁，見吾性之中焉，見吾性之和焉。推而致之，大本立，達道行，可以孚四方之觀聽矣。不然，遺實而徇名，略近而騖遠，周行之忽而旁
translation_en: …could this convergence in the course of the age be mere chance? Moreover, the scholars of the royal realm surely belong among those celebrated as illustrious and outstanding men. The eyes and ears of all quarters are fixed upon them. Thus, concerning the ways of august sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons, and concerning human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue, their methods are examined; concerning Heaven’s tokens and Earth’s sustaining breadth, what befits the people and the categories of things, and civil and military governance, their learning is examined; concerning their capacity to order and assist the workings of Heaven and Earth, comprehend them fully, and participate in their transforming and nourishing activity, their accomplishments are examined. Yet all these belong to our nature; they are not imparted from outside. Turn inward and seek: all things are complete within us. Thus, the nurturing of spiritual excellence, the plans and achievements of divine sages, and the expression of pure loyalty [?] reveal the equilibrium of our nature and the harmony of our nature. Extend these to their fullest realization, and the great foundation will be established and the universally followed Way put into practice, winning the confidence of those who watch and listen from every quarter. Otherwise, abandoning substance to pursue reputation, neglecting what is near to chase what is distant, disregarding the broad road and turning toward side…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
徑之惑且號曰是都人士也
亦罔而已爾席珍不佞不敢
以一第爲二三子榮而君子
成信之義主司敷求之責蓋
于是方有大懼也於戲休茲
尚知恤哉
河南開封府儒學敎授陳席
===
珍謹序
punctuated:
徑之惑，且號曰：「是都人士也。」亦罔而已爾。席珍不佞，不敢以一第爲二三子榮，而君子成信之義、主司敷求之責，蓋于是方有大懼也。於戲！休茲，尚知恤哉！
河南開封府儒學敎授陳席珍謹序。
translation_en:
…led astray by bypaths, yet proclaiming, “These are men of the capital”—this would be nothing but deception. I, Xizhen, lacking ability, dare not regard success in a single examination as glory for you gentlemen. Rather, it is precisely here that I feel great apprehension over the gentleman’s obligation to establish trustworthiness and the examination officials’ responsibility to seek worthy men far and wide. Ah! May you bring honor to this, and remain mindful of your responsibilities!
Respectfully prefaced by Chen Xizhen, Professor of the Confucian School of Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史桂榮〔君用江西上饒縣人壬午貢士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳則清〔君揚福建閩縣人丁丑進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右參議陳塏〔山甫浙江餘姚縣人壬辰進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使張素〔君賜直隸易州人辛巳進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事柯喬〔遷之直隸青陽縣人己丑進士〕
===
考試官
河南開封府儒學敎授陳席珍〔子聘福建候官縣人戊子貢士〕
福建興化府莆田縣儒學敎諭黃國奎〔子聚江西廬陵縣人丁酉貢士〕
同考試官

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十
而不惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七
十而從心所欲不踰矩
小德川流大德敦化此天地之所以爲大
也
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也詩云周道如砥其直如矢君子
===
所履小人所視
易
元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利者義之
和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁足以長
人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和義貞固
足以幹事君子行此四德者故曰乾元
亨利貞
允升大吉上合志也
神而明之存乎其人默而成之不言而信
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」

小德川流，大德敦化，此天地之所以爲大也。

夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。《詩》云：「周道如砥，其直如矢。君子所履，小人所視。」

易

元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁足以長人，嘉會足以合禮，利物足以和義，貞固足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」

允升，大吉，上合志也。

神而明之，存乎其人；默而成之，不言而信
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “At fifteen, I set my heart on learning. At thirty, I stood firm. At forty, I was free from perplexity. At fifty, I understood Heaven’s mandate. At sixty, my ear was attuned. At seventy, I followed my heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds.”

“Lesser virtue flows like streams; greater virtue brings forth abundant transformation. This is what makes Heaven and Earth great.”

“Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the noble man can follow this road and pass in and out through this gate. The Book of Odes says: ‘The road of Zhou is smooth as a whetstone, straight as an arrow. It is where the noble man treads and where the common people look.’”

Book of Changes

“Primal greatness is foremost among good qualities; success is the convergence of all that is excellent; benefit is the harmony of righteousness; constancy is the mainstay of affairs. By embodying benevolence, the noble man is able to lead others; by bringing excellence together, he is able to accord with ritual propriety; by benefiting things, he is able to harmonize righteousness; by being constant and firm, he is able to manage affairs. The noble man practices these four virtues. Hence it is said: ‘Qian: primal greatness, success, benefit, and constancy.’”

“‘Ascending with trust: great good fortune’ means that one’s aspirations accord with those above.”

“To apprehend its spiritual workings and make them clear depends upon the person; silently to bring it to completion, to inspire trust without speaking …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
存乎德行
與人同者物必歸焉故受之以大有有大
者不可以盈故受之以謙
書
成允成功惟汝賢克勤于邦克儉于家不
自滿假惟汝賢汝惟不矜天下莫與汝
爭能汝惟不伐天下莫與汝爭功
非知之艱行之惟艱王忱不艱允協于先
王成德
===
月之從星則以風雨
以佑乃辟永康兆民萬邦惟無斁
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻爲此春酒以介眉壽七月食
瓜八月斷壺九月叔苴采荼薪樗食我
農夫
無棄爾輔員于爾輻屢顧爾僕不輸爾載
終踰絕險曾是不意
punctuated:
存乎德行。

與人同者，物必歸焉，故受之以大有。有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙。

書

成允成功，惟汝賢；克勤于邦，克儉于家，不自滿假，惟汝賢。汝惟不矜，天下莫與汝爭能；汝惟不伐，天下莫與汝爭功。

非知之艱，行之惟艱。王忱不艱，允協于先王成德。

月之從星，則以風雨。

以佑乃辟，永康兆民，萬邦惟無斁。

詩

六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽。八月剝棗，十月穫稻。爲此春酒，以介眉壽。七月食瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴。采荼薪樗，食我農夫。

無棄爾輔，員于爾輻。屢顧爾僕，不輸爾載。終踰絕險，曾是不意。
translation_en:
…depends upon virtuous conduct.

When one joins in fellowship with others, things will necessarily come to one. Thus Fellowship with Others is followed by Great Possession. Those whose possessions are great must not become full of themselves; thus Great Possession is followed by Modesty.

Book of Documents

That your words are trustworthy and your undertakings successful is due to your worthiness. You can be diligent in affairs of state and frugal at home, without self-satisfaction or arrogance: this is your worthiness. Because you do not vaunt yourself, no one under Heaven contests your ability; because you do not boast, no one under Heaven contests your achievements.

It is not knowing that is difficult; putting knowledge into practice is difficult. If the king is sincere, this will not be difficult, and he will truly accord with the perfected virtue of the former kings.

When the moon follows the stars, wind and rain result.

Thereby assist your sovereign and secure lasting peace for the myriad people, so that the myriad states never grow weary.

Book of Odes

In the sixth month we eat bush cherries and wild grapes; in the seventh month we boil mallows and beans. In the eighth month we beat down jujubes; in the tenth month we harvest rice. With it we make spring ale to promote long life. In the seventh month we eat melons; in the eighth month we cut gourds; in the ninth month we gather hemp seeds. We gather bitter herbs and cut tree-of-heaven wood for fuel, feeding our farmers.

Do not discard your chariot’s side supports; reinforce its spokes. Look often to your driver, lest your load fall off. You will finally cross the most perilous terrain—yet you give no thought to this.

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽考遐不作人
我其夙夜畏天之威于時保之
春秋
元年隱公元年桓公
公子遂如齊宣公元年仲孫蔑會齊高固
于無婁宣公十有五年公會晉侯衞侯
鄭伯曹伯宋世子成齊國佐邾人同盟
于戚成公十有五年公會晉侯齊侯宋
公衞侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子于商任襄
===
公二十有一年冬公會晉侯齊侯宋公
衞侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子薛伯杞伯小
邾子于沙隨襄公二十有二年衞侯之
弟鱄出奔晉襄公二十有七年楚公子
比出奔晉昭公元年夏四月楚公子比
自晉歸于楚昭公十有三年
冬公孫歸父如齊宣公十年
公會晉侯宋公衞侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世
子光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭襄公
punctuated:
倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？
我其夙夜，畏天之威，于時保之。
春秋
「元年。」隱公。「元年。」桓公。
「公子遂如齊。」宣公元年。「仲孫蔑會齊高固于無婁。」宣公十有五年。「公會晉侯、衞侯、鄭伯、曹伯、宋世子成、齊國佐、邾人，同盟于戚。」成公十有五年。「公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衞侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子于商任。」襄公二十有一年。「冬，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衞侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于沙隨。」襄公二十有二年。「衞侯之弟鱄出奔晉。」襄公二十有七年。「楚公子比出奔晉。」昭公元年。「夏，四月，楚公子比自晉歸于楚。」昭公十有三年。
「冬，公孫歸父如齊。」宣公十年。
「公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。」襄公
translation_en:
Resplendent is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in heaven. Long-lived is the king of Zhou; would he not nurture worthy men?
From dawn to night, let us stand in awe of Heaven’s might, and thereby preserve what we hold.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The first year.” Duke Yin. “The first year.” Duke Huan.
“Prince Sui went to Qi.” First year of Duke Xuan. “Zhongsun Mie met Gao Gu of Qi at Wulou.” Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan. “The duke met the marquises of Jin and Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, Cheng, heir apparent of Song, Guo Zuo of Qi, and men of Zhu; they concluded a joint covenant at Qi.” Fifteenth year of Duke Cheng. “The duke met the marquises of Jin and Qi, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, and the viscounts of Ju and Zhu at Shangren.” Twenty-first year of Duke Xiang. “In winter, the duke met the marquises of Jin and Qi, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, the viscounts of Ju and Zhu, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Lesser Zhu at Shasui.” Twenty-second year of Duke Xiang. “Zhuan, younger brother of the marquis of Wei, fled to Jin.” Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang. “Prince Bi of Chu fled to Jin.” First year of Duke Zhao. “In summer, in the fourth month, Prince Bi of Chu returned from Jin to Chu.” Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.
“In winter, Gongsun Guifu went to Qi.” Tenth year of Duke Xuan.
“The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, the viscounts of Ju and Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscount of Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng.” Duke Xiang …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
〔十年〕公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭〔襄公十有一年〕夏叔孫豹會晉趙武
楚屈建蔡公孫歸生衛石惡陳孔奐鄭
良霄許人曹人于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戌衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
罕虎許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕
禮記
===
正室守大廟尊宗室而君臣之道著矣
禮之所尊尊其義也失其義陳其數祝史
之事也故其數可陳也其義難知也知
其義而敬守之天子之所以治天下也
然則先王之爲樂也以法治也善則行象
德矣
用之於戰勝則無敵用之於禮義則順治
外無敵內順治此之謂盛德
第貳場
punctuated:
〔十年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔襄公十有一年〕夏，叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋。〔襄公二十有七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。〔昭公元年〕

禮記

正室守大廟，尊宗室而君臣之道著矣。

禮之所尊，尊其義也。失其義，陳其數，祝史之事也。故其數可陳也，其義難知也。知其義而敬守之，天子之所以治天下也。

然則先王之爲樂也，以法治也。善則行象德矣。

用之於戰勝則無敵，用之於禮義則順治。外無敵，內順治，此之謂盛德。

第貳場
translation_en:
…〔Tenth year.〕The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng.〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕In summer, Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao at Song.〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao at Guo.〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

The principal heir keeps charge of the grand ancestral temple. By honoring the principal ancestral line, the proper relationship between ruler and minister is made manifest.

What ritual honors is its meaning. To lose that meaning and merely set forth its forms is the business of invocators and scribes. Thus, its forms can be set forth, but its meaning is difficult to understand. To understand its meaning and reverently preserve it is the means by which the Son of Heaven governs all under Heaven.

Thus, when the former kings made music, they used it to give a pattern to government. When it is good, its performance represents virtue.

Applied to victory in war, it leaves none able to withstand it; applied to ritual and righteousness, it brings harmony and order. To meet no opposition abroad and to have harmony and order at home: this is called consummate virtue.

Second Session

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
論
天地聖人之常
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良文學詔〔元光元年〕
擬唐以魏徵為太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬
賜免承天等府田租湖廣守臣謝表
判語〔五條〕
同僚代判署文案
===
棄毀器物稼穡等
見任官輒自立碑
禁經斷人充宿衛
官吏詞訟家人訴
第參場
策五道
問自古帝王創造鴻業以六合為家矣然
於肇迹之所鑾輿再過必錫宴父老賜
復湯沐恩賚蓋獨被焉或又發為詩文
punctuated:
論
天地聖人之常。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良文學詔〔元光元年〕。
擬唐以魏徵為太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕。
擬賜免承天等府田租，湖廣守臣謝表。

判語〔五條〕
同僚代判署文案。
棄毀器物稼穡等。
見任官輒自立碑。
禁經斷人充宿衛。
官吏詞訟家人訴。

第參場
策五道
問：自古帝王創造鴻業，以六合為家矣。然於肇迹之所，鑾輿再過，必錫宴父老，賜復湯沐，恩賚蓋獨被焉。或又發為詩文，
translation_en:
Discourse
The constancy of Heaven, Earth, and the sages.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials [one topic from among these [?]]
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty calling for the recommendation of men of worth, integrity, and literary learning [first year of Yuanguang].
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent [sixteenth year of Zhenguan].
Compose a memorial of thanks by an official serving in Huguang for the imperial remission of land taxes in Chengtian and other prefectures.

Legal judgments [five items]
A fellow official acting in another’s place to render judgments and sign case documents.
Discarding or destroying utensils, crops, and the like.
An incumbent official erecting a commemorative stele for himself without authorization.
The prohibition against employing convicted persons as palace guards.
Family members bringing complaints in litigation involving officials or subofficial functionaries.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings have founded great enterprises, taking all within the six directions as their home. Yet whenever the imperial carriage again passed through the place where their rise began, they invariably bestowed banquets upon its elders and granted exemptions and bathing allowances [?]; their gracious rewards thus fell especially upon that place. Some also expressed their feelings in poetry and prose …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以寄情眷昭奕史冊如漢高帝沛上之
歌唐太宗慶善宮之詩蓋其最著也亦
皆有可取者乎我
太祖高皇帝自
中都還經滁陽有感舊記之作其中意指所
述可得聞乎亦有高出前代之外者乎
皇上肇迹
興都入繼
大統已而
===
大狩龍飛恭卜
寢園
達孝至仁三代而下未有也其
御製則有思恩之賦閱
純德山再閱
顯陵之歌及
諭父老恩詔諸文雖典謨風雅何以加焉今可
舉而盡言之乎
天章睿藻上繼
punctuated: 以寄情眷，昭奕史冊，如漢高帝沛上之歌、唐太宗慶善宮之詩，蓋其最著也。亦皆有可取者乎？我太祖高皇帝自中都還，經滁陽，有感舊記之作，其中意指所述，可得聞乎？亦有高出前代之外者乎？皇上肇迹興都，入繼大統，已而大狩龍飛，恭卜寢園，達孝至仁，三代而下未有也。其御製則有思恩之賦、閱純德山再閱顯陵之歌，及諭父老恩詔諸文，雖典謨風雅，何以加焉？今可舉而盡言之乎？天章睿藻，上繼
translation_en:
…to convey their affection and attachment, shining splendidly in the historical records. Emperor Gao of Han’s song at Pei and Emperor Taizong of Tang’s poem on Qingshan Palace are perhaps the most celebrated examples. Do they all possess qualities worthy of appreciation? Our Emperor Taizu Gao, returning from Zhongdu through Chuyang, composed a Record of Reflections on the Past. May we hear what intentions and ideas it expresses? Does it also contain qualities surpassing those of earlier dynasties?

His Majesty began his rise in Xingdu and came to succeed to the imperial throne. Subsequently, he made a great imperial tour to the place of his rise and reverently selected the site for the imperial mausoleum grounds. Such consummate filial piety and supreme benevolence have been unequalled since the Three Dynasties. His imperial compositions include the rhapsody Reflecting on Parental Kindness, the songs on viewing Mount Chunde and viewing Xianling again, and such writings as his gracious edict addressed to the elders. How could even the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents, or the Airs and Odes of the Book of Poetry, surpass these? Can you now enumerate them and discuss them fully? His celestial compositions and sagely literary works carry forward the legacy of…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
高皇遠邁千古固如是矣其亦有所本而然歟
爾都人士衣被且久其敬鋪張揚厲之
問禹貢荆州厥田下中厥賦上下賦加于
田五等厥貢亦為九州最今湖賦長沙
為重尚殺於蘇湖貢則羽毛之外於古
所稱皆無之所不及於古者何歟古人
有謂荆陽地廣饒財而訾窳偷生者有
因土地埆瘠而云不止武昌居者又有
云鄂土沃而民剽者然則今之肥瘠登
===
耗果若誰所云者歟自今言之其賦于
民者實二百十萬有奇耳兌運撥運之
外所以贍內地者無幾矣計一年之全
入僅支一年之用
聖天子軫念豐鎬屢
賜免租惠至渥也則夫所入益寡其不足之
數將何以為取盈者歟
親藩環楚而王者八枝葉日益繁數十年後
將何以為制祿者歟制貢之法則有額
punctuated:
高皇，遠邁千古，固如是矣。其亦有所本而然歟？爾都人士衣被且久，其敬鋪張揚厲之。

問：禹貢荆州，厥田下中，厥賦上下，賦加于田五等，厥貢亦為九州最。今湖賦長沙為重，尚殺於蘇湖；貢則羽毛之外，於古所稱皆無之。所不及於古者何歟？古人有謂荆陽地廣饒財，而訾窳偷生者；有因土地埆瘠而云不止武昌居者；又有云鄂土沃而民剽者。然則今之肥瘠登耗，果若誰所云者歟？自今言之，其賦于民者實二百十萬有奇耳。兌運、撥運之外，所以贍內地者無幾矣。計一年之全入，僅支一年之用。聖天子軫念豐鎬，屢賜免租，惠至渥也。則夫所入益寡，其不足之數，將何以為取盈者歟？親藩環楚而王者八，枝葉日益繁，數十年後，將何以為制祿者歟？制貢之法，則有額
translation_en:
…Emperor Gao, far surpassing all past ages: this is indeed so. Yet must there not also be a foundation from which this springs? You gentlemen of this capital have long enjoyed his beneficence; reverently expound and extol it.

Question: In the Tribute of Yu, Jingzhou’s fields were ranked lower-middle and its tax contribution upper-lower: its tax rank exceeded its field rank by five grades. Its tribute was also the greatest among the Nine Provinces. Today, among the tax burdens of Huguang, Changsha’s is the heaviest, yet it is still lighter than those of Suzhou and Huzhou. As for tribute, apart from feathers and hides, none of the items named in antiquity is now supplied. Why does it fall short of antiquity? Some ancient writers said that Jingzhou and Yangzhou had extensive lands and abundant resources, yet their people were idle and merely eked out a living. Another, speaking of the land’s barrenness, said that one should not remain in Wuchang [?]. Still another said that the soil of E was fertile but its people were fierce. Whose account, then, actually accords with the fertility or barrenness and the abundance or scarcity of today?

Speaking of the present, the taxes levied on the people in fact amount to only a little over 2,100,000. After the grain shipments transferred to transport crews and those dispatched by allocation, little remains to support the province’s interior. The entire revenue of one year barely covers one year’s expenditure. The sagely Son of Heaven, solicitous for Feng and Hao, has repeatedly granted tax remissions: his favor is most generous. Yet receipts thereby become still smaller. How, then, is the shortfall to be made up? Eight princes of the imperial house hold princely establishments throughout Chu, and their descendants grow more numerous daily. Several decades hence, how are their stipends to be provided? Under the regulations governing tribute, there are fixed quotas…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
辦有派辦不容免矣其他若馬船之直
漕艘之費及湖中泛應之需務舉其恒
議盡其凡一不備則糾之以例有可以
節損之者歟大木之採辦不貲平蠻之
賞餉亦鉅司農調贓罰以濟邊司馬取
徒贖以募士督逋之部使相望催輸之
部檄麏至一不應則繩之以法有可以
劑量之者歟即今江漢水溢千里潰防
田廬漂沒盜竊且作玆惟賑恤之議矣
===
其何以爲征科之地歟伊欲使貢賦修
而上足利國惠澤流而下不病民何施
而可夫生於其地者必知其地之故酌
古準今佇聞高論
問楚之勳業文章自古斌斌盛矣而倡道
舂陵以上接孟氏則自濂溪周子始論
者謂其不由師傳默契道體今所著圖
說易通固在也果與易書春秋語孟相
出入歟而其言何者爲至要歟或疑其
punctuated:
辦有派，辦不容免矣。其他若馬船之直、漕艘之費及湖中泛應之需，務舉其恒，議盡其凡，一不備則糾之以例，有可以節損之者歟？大木之採辦不貲，平蠻之賞餉亦鉅。司農調贓罰以濟邊，司馬取徒贖以募士，督逋之部使相望，催輸之部檄麏至，一不應則繩之以法，有可以劑量之者歟？即今江漢水溢，千里潰防，田廬漂沒，盜竊且作，玆惟賑恤之議矣，其何以爲征科之地歟？伊欲使貢賦修而上足利國，惠澤流而下不病民，何施而可？夫生於其地者必知其地之故，酌古準今，佇聞高論。

問：楚之勳業文章，自古斌斌盛矣。而倡道舂陵，以上接孟氏，則自濂溪周子始。論者謂其不由師傳，默契道體。今所著《圖說》《易通》固在也，果與《易》《書》《春秋》《語》《孟》相出入歟？而其言何者爲至要歟？或疑其
translation_en:
…Procurement is apportioned by assignment, and these obligations cannot be waived. Other demands include the cost of horses and boats, the expenses of grain-transport vessels, and miscellaneous requisitions in Huguang. The standing requirements must all be met, and every category fully considered; if even one is not provided for, the regulations are invoked to hold officials accountable. Are there any expenditures that could be reduced? Procuring large timbers costs immense sums, as do the rewards and military provisions for suppressing the Man peoples. The Minister of Revenue transfers confiscated funds and fines to support the frontier; the Minister of War uses payments for redeeming penal-servitude sentences to recruit soldiers. Ministry envoys supervising the collection of arrears follow one another in an unbroken succession, and ministry dispatches demanding remittances arrive in droves. Failure to meet even one demand brings punishment under the law. Is there any way to adjust these demands to available means? Just now, the Jiang and Han rivers have overflowed, embankments have collapsed across a thousand li, fields and dwellings have been swept away or submerged, and theft is beginning to spread. At such a time, relief is surely the matter to discuss. How can this be a region from which to exact taxes and levies? If we wish tribute and taxes to be duly supplied, sufficiently benefiting the state above, while beneficence flows down without distressing the people below, what measures will accomplish this? Those born in a region must know its circumstances. Weigh the past against the present; we await your illuminating discussions.

Question: Chu has abounded in distinguished achievements and literary accomplishment since antiquity. Yet it was Master Zhou of Lianxi who first proclaimed the Way at Chongling and carried forward the lineage of Mencius. Commentators say that, without receiving instruction from a teacher, he attained a silent understanding of the substance of the Way. His Explanation of the Diagram (Tushuo) and Penetrating the Changes (Yitong) are still extant. Do they indeed accord with the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Analects, and the Mencius? Which of his statements are the most essential? Some doubt that his…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
說本於老子或謂圖傳之穆修或又謂
出於壽涯信斯言也則亦有師矣而何
以謂之默契歟其學授之二程則每令
尋仲尼顏子樂處所樂何事蓋引而不
發者也今可得而言之歟黃太史稱其
光風霽月而明道一再見即吟風弄月
以歸是樂也亦有同於孔顏否歟明道
之得於師者如此伊川乃謂其得不傳
之學於遺經而一言不及濂溪此又何
===
歟明道亦曰吾學雖有所受天理二字
却是自家體貼出來豈樂之外復有所
謂天理歟夫默契授受之間蓋必有說
而生其鄉不知其學吾實恥之故願諸
君之深言之也
問春秋之義以尊王為正故當時之圖霸
者莫不藉是以求服乎諸侯下此則三
國之雄亦知斯之為足以濟也然周之
不西漢之不東君子不能無憾焉乃若
punctuated:
說本於老子，或謂圖傳之穆修，或又謂出於壽涯。信斯言也，則亦有師矣，而何以謂之默契歟？其學授之二程，則每令尋仲尼、顏子樂處，所樂何事？蓋引而不發者也，今可得而言之歟？黃太史稱其光風霽月，而明道一再見，即吟風弄月以歸，是樂也，亦有同於孔顏否歟？明道之得於師者如此，伊川乃謂其得不傳之學於遺經，而一言不及濂溪，此又何歟？明道亦曰：「吾學雖有所受，天理二字却是自家體貼出來。」豈樂之外復有所謂天理歟？夫默契授受之間，蓋必有說，而生其鄉，不知其學，吾實恥之，故願諸君之深言之也。

問：春秋之義，以尊王為正，故當時之圖霸者，莫不藉是以求服乎諸侯。下此則三國之雄，亦知斯之為足以濟也。然周之不西、漢之不東，君子不能無憾焉。乃若
translation_en:
…his teachings were based on Laozi; some say that the Diagram was transmitted by Mu Xiu, and others that it came from Shou Ya [?]. If these statements are true, then he too had a teacher. How, then, can he be said to have attained a tacit understanding? When he transmitted his learning to the two Cheng brothers, he repeatedly instructed them to seek what Zhongni (Confucius) and Master Yan took joy in. What was it that they enjoyed? This was surely a case of drawing the bow without releasing the arrow. Can its meaning now be put into words? Grand Scribe Huang praised him as a “clear breeze and a moon after rain.” After meeting him only once or twice, Mingdao returned home chanting of the breeze and sporting with the moon. Did this joy also have something in common with that of Confucius and Yan Hui? Such was what Mingdao gained from his teacher. Yet Yichuan said that he had acquired learning whose transmission had been lost from the surviving classics, without mentioning Lianxi at all. Why was this? Mingdao also said: “Although some of my learning was received from others, the two words ‘Heavenly principle’ were something I worked out through my own understanding.” Could there be something called Heavenly principle apart from this joy? Surely there must be an explanation of the relationship between tacit understanding and the transmission and reception of learning. To have been born in his native region yet not to understand his learning is something I truly find shameful. I therefore wish you gentlemen to discuss it in depth.

Question: The principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals take honoring the king as their proper standard. Thus, those who sought hegemony in that age invariably invoked this to secure the submission of the regional lords. In later times, the powerful leaders of the Three Kingdoms likewise knew that this could suffice to accomplish their aims. Yet the failure of the Zhou to return west and of the Han to return east cannot but occasion regret among gentlemen. As for…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其事機之失得人品之高下則間有可
疑者姑舉數端較之齊桓徴師以伐楚
魏武會獵以懼吳一也何以强楚而見
屈以弱吳而取勝耶江黄與盟以謀楚
吳蜀同仇以拒魏一也何齊不救黄之
滅吳不救蜀之亡耶用孟明而秦霸成
誅得臣而晋憂釋以成敗之幾難料也
何馬謖之一敗知後效之不可冀耶欒
書還繞角之師荀罃致偪陽之績以進
===
退之權在將也何辛毗之一來使元帥
之不敢動耶管鮑之相知也而不共君
亮統之齊名也而不同國何不審於擇
君之初致委曲以相徇耶晏嬰之知孔
也而敢肆侮周瑜之知亮也而輒相圖
何不思夫引君之術致無成以自悔耶
荀彧之料人賈詡之料敵中矣何伍參
之嬖曹劌之賤亦足以致多筭之勝耶
子貢之存魯子產之寛鄭善矣何趙咨
punctuated: 其事機之失得、人品之高下，則間有可疑者，姑舉數端較之。齊桓徴師以伐楚，魏武會獵以懼吳，一也。何以强楚而見屈，以弱吳而取勝耶？江黄與盟以謀楚，吳蜀同仇以拒魏，一也。何齊不救黄之滅，吳不救蜀之亡耶？用孟明而秦霸成，誅得臣而晋憂釋，以成敗之幾難料也。何馬謖之一敗，知後效之不可冀耶？欒書還繞角之師，荀罃致偪陽之績，以進退之權在將也。何辛毗之一來，使元帥之不敢動耶？管鮑之相知也，而不共君；亮統之齊名也，而不同國。何不審於擇君之初，致委曲以相徇耶？晏嬰之知孔也，而敢肆侮；周瑜之知亮也，而輒相圖。何不思夫引君之術，致無成以自悔耶？荀彧之料人，賈詡之料敵，中矣。何伍參之嬖、曹劌之賤，亦足以致多筭之勝耶？子貢之存魯，子產之寛鄭，善矣。何趙咨
translation_en:
…As for their successes and failures in responding to circumstances, and the relative quality of their characters, there are points that invite doubt. Let us take a few instances and compare them. Duke Huan of Qi summoned troops to attack Chu; Emperor Wu of Wei called for a joint hunt to intimidate Wu. These were alike. Why was mighty Chu brought to submit, while weak Wu gained victory? Jiang and Huang joined an alliance to plot against Chu; Wu and Shu opposed a common enemy in resisting Wei. These were alike. Why did Qi not save Huang from destruction, and Wu not save Shu from extinction? By employing Mengming, Qin established its hegemony; by executing Dechen, Chu relieved Jin of its anxiety. This shows how difficult it is to foresee the incipient causes of success and failure. Why, then, was a single defeat by Ma Su enough to establish that no subsequent service could be hoped for from him? Luan Shu withdrew his army from Raojiao, while Xun Ying achieved victory at Biyang: authority over advance and retreat rested with the general. Why, then, did Xin Pi’s arrival alone make the commander-in-chief dare not move?

Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya understood one another, yet did not serve the same lord; Zhuge Liang and Pang Tong enjoyed equal renown, yet did not belong to the same state [?]. Why did they not exercise discernment when first choosing a lord, thereby coming to compromise themselves in accommodating others? Yan Ying recognized Confucius’s worth, yet dared to heap insults upon him; Zhou Yu recognized Zhuge Liang’s worth, yet repeatedly plotted against him. Why did they not consider how to guide their rulers, thereby accomplishing nothing and leaving themselves cause for regret? Xun Yu was accurate in judging men, and Jia Xu in judging the enemy. How, then, could Wu Can, a favored courtier, and Cao Gui, a man of low station, likewise achieve victories through superior calculation? Zigong’s preservation of Lu and Zichan’s lenient governance of Zheng were admirable. How, then, could Zhao Zi …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之誇鄧芝之往亦足以致不辱之譽耶
使生當其時用居其地事必何如而權
其中人必何如而取其則固必有道矣
願酌言之以觀尚友之志
問川湖貴竹之徼西南夷之墟古稱槃瓠
種落其降才爾殊矣在古禹功畢而三
苗敘周道興而蠻荆威治之上也秦置
黔中漢開牂牁唐分巫敘宋列誓州有
得於制御之道否耶况蠻蜑開春申之
===
宅壺頭肇伏波之祠銅柱鐫李皐之銘
降臺勒李誦之記非無震讋之者而或
者以爲雖唐虞之仁不能柔秦漢之勇
不能威者何耶我
太祖高皇帝疆理天下凡蠻夷戎貊悉置酋長
若采衛然域以山谿寛其法網即敘之
道不治之略盡矣我
皇上敷文詰武交南來庭其在中邦罔不懷畏
乃今蠟爾一山絞苗出沒擾我疆邑彼
punctuated:
之誇、鄧芝之往，亦足以致不辱之譽耶？使生當其時，用居其地，事必何如而權其中，人必何如而取其則？固必有道矣，願酌言之，以觀尚友之志。
問：川湖貴竹之徼，西南夷之墟，古稱槃瓠種落，其降才爾殊矣。在古，禹功畢而三苗敘，周道興而蠻荆威，治之上也。秦置黔中，漢開牂牁，唐分巫敘，宋列誓州，有得於制御之道否耶？况蠻蜑開春申之宅，壺頭肇伏波之祠，銅柱鐫李皐之銘，降臺勒李誦之記，非無震讋之者。而或者以爲，雖唐虞之仁不能柔，秦漢之勇不能威者，何耶？我太祖高皇帝疆理天下，凡蠻夷戎貊，悉置酋長，若采衛然，域以山谿，寛其法網，即敘之道、不治之略盡矣。我皇上敷文詰武，交南來庭，其在中邦罔不懷畏。乃今蠟爾一山，絞苗出沒，擾我疆邑，彼
translation_en:
…the boasts of Zhao Zi and the mission of Deng Zhi likewise suffice to earn them reputations for having upheld their states’ honor? If you candidates had lived in those times and held office in those places, how would you have weighed affairs to find the proper course, and how would you have selected men to serve as your models? Surely there must be a way. Please offer a considered account, so that we may observe your aspiration to befriend the worthy of antiquity.
Question: On the frontiers of Chuan, Hu, and Guizhu—the lands of the southwestern peoples—live the tribal groups anciently called the descendants of Panhu. The capacities bestowed upon them are so different! In antiquity, when Yu’s labors were completed, the Sanmiao were brought into order; when the Way of Zhou flourished, the Man of Jing were awed into submission. These were the highest achievements of government. The Qin established Qianzhong; the Han opened up Zangke; the Tang divided Wu and Xu; and the Song set out Shi prefectures [?]. Did these measures attain the proper way of controlling and governing them? Moreover, among the Man and Dan the residence of Lord Chunshen was established; at Hutou a shrine to the General Who Calms the Waves was founded; a bronze pillar bore an inscription by Li Gao; and a surrender terrace bore a record by Li Song [?]. It is not that there have been none who struck terror into them. Yet some maintain that even the benevolence of Tang Yao and Yu Shun could not win them over, nor the valor of the Qin and Han overawe them. Why is this?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao laid out the boundaries and administrative divisions of All under Heaven. Among all the Man, Yi, Rong, and Mo peoples he appointed chieftains, as in the ancient Cai and Wei zones. He bounded their territories by mountains and streams and relaxed the constraints of the law. Thus the means of bringing them into order and the strategy of governing without direct intervention were fully realized. Our present Emperor spreads civil culture and puts military affairs in order. Jiaonan comes to court, and within the central realm there are none who do not cherish his favor and fear his might. Yet now, on the single mountain of La’er, the Jiao Miao [?] appear and disappear, harassing our frontier settlements. They …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
獨何所恃而然耶夫環而控制之者永
順保靖酉陽三司也其鎭筸平茶五寨
諸司則錯而抗扼之者也乃縱蠟爾山
之惡而不爲之所彼亦何所挾而然耶
蓋昔者嘗有徵調於諸司矣往無弗克
今環視諸苗而不動若曰諸司昔用苗
以成功今籍苗以嫁惡則豈世忠之謂
耶即今仰煩
聖慮間遣重臣相機决策用申
===
天威督府經略之餘具有蕩平之緒矣不知善
後之圖使彼若南人不復反者必如何
而後可
punctuated: 獨何所恃而然耶？夫環而控制之者，永順、保靖、酉陽三司也。其鎭筸、平茶、五寨諸司，則錯而抗扼之者也。乃縱蠟爾山之惡，而不爲之所，彼亦何所挾而然耶？蓋昔者嘗有徵調於諸司矣，往無弗克。今環視諸苗而不動，若曰諸司昔用苗以成功，今籍苗以嫁惡，則豈世忠之謂耶？即今仰煩聖慮，間遣重臣，相機决策，用申天威。督府經略之餘，具有蕩平之緒矣。不知善後之圖，使彼若南人不復反者，必如何而後可？
translation_en:
…what, then, do they alone rely upon to act in this way? The three native offices of Yongshun, Baojing, and Youyang surround and hold them in check. The offices of Zhen’gan, Pingcha, Wuzhai, and the others are interspersed among them to oppose them and block their routes. Yet they allow the evildoers of La’er Mountain free rein and take no measures against them. What backing do they, too, possess that enables them to act thus? In the past, troops were requisitioned from these offices, and wherever they went they prevailed. Now they look around at the various Miao groups without taking action. If it is said that these offices formerly employed the Miao to achieve success but now use the Miao to shift blame onto others, can this be called loyalty maintained through the generations?

Now this matter has troubled His Majesty’s sagely deliberations, and senior ministers have been dispatched from time to time to assess circumstances and determine policy, thereby asserting imperial might. Through the supreme commander’s strategic efforts, the beginnings of complete pacification are already in place. But as for planning the subsequent settlement, what must be done to ensure that these people, like the people of the south, never rebel again?

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十
而不惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七
十而從心所欲不踰矩
高啓
同考試官敎諭楊批聖人始終心學此作得之
同考試官學正歐陽批平淡可誦
同考試官敎授金批達孔子獨覺其進之意
===
考試官敎諭黃批明潔
考試官敎授陳批雅馴
聖人自名其進德始于學而成于化也夫聖人
之德非積而化也而其自名猶志學以馴至焉
夫人可以不自勉哉昔夫子年踰七十自覺其
德之所至而爲之言曰吾今之有得非一日之
積也學而不息焉耳夫學先於立志也吾自十
五蓋銳然有作聖之志矣大學之道篤好焉而
爲之不厭也學貴於能守也吾年三十蓋卓然
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」
高啓
同考試官敎諭楊批：「聖人始終心學，此作得之。」
同考試官學正歐陽批：「平淡可誦。」
同考試官敎授金批：「達孔子獨覺其進之意。」
考試官敎諭黃批：「明潔。」
考試官敎授陳批：「雅馴。」
聖人自名其進德，始于學而成于化也。夫聖人之德，非積而化也，而其自名，猶志學以馴至焉。夫人可以不自勉哉？昔夫子年踰七十，自覺其德之所至，而爲之言曰：「吾今之有得，非一日之積也，學而不息焉耳。夫學先於立志也。吾自十五，蓋銳然有作聖之志矣。大學之道，篤好焉而爲之不厭也。學貴於能守也。吾年三十，蓋卓然
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
The Master said: “At fifteen I set my mind on learning; at thirty I stood firm; at forty I was free from perplexity; at fifty I understood Heaven’s mandate; at sixty my ear was attuned; at seventy I followed my heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds.”
Gao Qi
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The sage’s learning of the mind, from beginning to end—this composition captures it.”
Associate Examiner Ouyang, School Instructor, comments: “Plain and unadorned, and pleasing to recite.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Professor, comments: “Conveys the meaning of Confucius’s own inward awareness of his progress.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Clear and clean.”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Elegant and polished.”
In describing his own advancement in virtue, the sage begins with learning and culminates in transformation. The sage’s virtue does not attain transformation through accumulation; yet in his own account, he still speaks of setting his mind on learning and gradually reaching that point. Can anyone, then, fail to exert himself?
Formerly, when the Master was over seventy, he perceived the level his virtue had reached and spoke of it thus: “What I have attained today is not the accumulation of a single day; it is simply the result of learning without cease. In learning, establishing one’s resolve comes first. From the age of fifteen, I already had an ardent resolve to become a sage. I loved devotedly the Way of the Great Learning and practiced it tirelessly. In learning, what matters is being able to hold fast. At thirty, I was already firmly …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有自立之操矣道心為主貞固焉而守之不失
也由是而四十焉極深而研幾其於萬物之備
自明察其當然之理矣由是而五十焉盡性以
至命其於萬理之會自默契其從出之原矣至
於六十則神明為之内蘊入於耳而通於心無
適而非道也何待思而後得耶至於七十則大
用為之顯行由乎中而應乎外從容以中矩也
何待勉而後中耶夫子自言其進德之序如此
夫自十五而七十心與年運忘身之老也自志
===
學而從心德以年邵與天為一也蓋獨覺其進
而因以自名其示學者以進修之階歟抑夫子
嘗曰若聖與仁則吾豈敢而至此則仁聖非所
辭矣而說者以為謙何耶蓋德進固學而不厭
之驗而推之則其誨人不倦之心也然聖人於
此豈遂以為足哉俛焉孳孳終其身焉耳學者
未少有得而遽自滿假宜聖人之不可幾也
小德川流大德敦化此天地之所以為大
也
punctuated:
有自立之操矣。道心為主，貞固焉而守之不失也。由是而四十焉，極深而研幾，其於萬物之備，自明察其當然之理矣。由是而五十焉，盡性以至命，其於萬理之會，自默契其從出之原矣。至於六十，則神明為之内蘊，入於耳而通於心，無適而非道也，何待思而後得耶？至於七十，則大用為之顯行，由乎中而應乎外，從容以中矩也，何待勉而後中耶？夫子自言其進德之序如此。夫自十五而七十，心與年運，忘身之老也；自志學而從心，德以年邵，與天為一也。蓋獨覺其進，而因以自名，其示學者以進修之階歟？抑夫子嘗曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？」而至此，則仁聖非所辭矣，而說者以為謙，何耶？蓋德進固學而不厭之驗，而推之，則其誨人不倦之心也。然聖人於此，豈遂以為足哉？俛焉孳孳，終其身焉耳。學者未少有得，而遽自滿假，宜聖人之不可幾也。

小德川流，大德敦化，此天地之所以為大也。
translation_en:
…had acquired the resolve to stand firm on my own. Taking the moral mind as my master, I held steadfastly to it without letting it slip. From this I reached forty: probing the depths and investigating the subtle beginnings of things, I clearly discerned the principles governing how all the myriad things ought to be. From this I reached fifty: fully realizing my nature and thereby arriving at Heaven’s mandate, I inwardly apprehended the source from which all principles issue and in which they converge. At sixty, spiritual understanding was stored within me: whatever entered my ears penetrated my heart, and wherever I turned, there was nothing that was not the Way. Why should I have needed reflection before attaining understanding? At seventy, its great functioning became manifest in action: proceeding from within and responding to what lay outside, I effortlessly conformed to the rules. Why should I have needed exertion before hitting the mark?

Such was the Master’s own account of the stages by which he advanced in virtue. From fifteen to seventy, his mind progressed with his years, and he forgot the aging of his body. From setting his heart on learning to following his heart’s desires, his virtue grew loftier with age, becoming one with Heaven. Surely he alone perceived this progress and accordingly described himself: was this to show learners the successive steps of moral cultivation? Yet the Master once said, “As for sagehood and humaneness, how would I dare claim them?” By this point, however, humaneness and sagehood were no longer things he disclaimed. Why, then, do interpreters regard his words as modesty? His advance in virtue was certainly proof of his tireless learning; considered further, it also expressed his heart’s untiring commitment to teaching others. Yet did the sage therefore consider this sufficient? He simply labored diligently to the end of his life. Learners become complacent before gaining even a little understanding. No wonder sagehood remains beyond their reach!

“Lesser virtue flows like streams; greater virtue brings forth abundant transformation. This is what makes Heaven and Earth great.”

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
童承契
考試官教諭黃批說德之大小處最明此正
造化妙用見聖人之合德也
考試官教授陳批場中作者率以體用講小
德大德惟此作為得其指
中庸原造化所由大以見聖人之大也夫天地
之大大於德也非德則幾乎息矣而何以為大
耶觀於是則見聖人矣中庸三十章言天道也
意蓋曰擬仲尼於天地謂夫天地之大也然天
===
地亦於何而求之是故覆載之間物固不相害
矣道固不相悖矣所以然者小德之川流焉耳
感元化以屈伸而散殊之有象乘氣機以出入
而推行之有常蓋如川之流脉絡分明而往不
息也物固竝育矣道固竝行矣所以然者大德
之敦化焉耳陰陽藏其宅而絪縕為之用太極
統其體而闔闢為之樞蓋敦厚其化根本盛大
而出無窮也夫小德以為之分則富有之業足
以見天地之全功大德以為之本則不貳之眞
punctuated:
童承契

考試官教諭黃批：說德之大小處最明，此正造化妙用，見聖人之合德也。

考試官教授陳批：場中作者率以體用講小德大德，惟此作為得其指。

中庸原造化所由大，以見聖人之大也。夫天地之大，大於德也。非德則幾乎息矣，而何以為大耶？觀於是，則見聖人矣。中庸三十章言天道也，意蓋曰：擬仲尼於天地，謂夫天地之大也。然天地亦於何而求之？是故覆載之間，物固不相害矣，道固不相悖矣。所以然者，小德之川流焉耳。感元化以屈伸，而散殊之有象；乘氣機以出入，而推行之有常。蓋如川之流，脉絡分明而往不息也。物固竝育矣，道固竝行矣。所以然者，大德之敦化焉耳。陰陽藏其宅，而絪縕為之用；太極統其體，而闔闢為之樞。蓋敦厚其化，根本盛大而出無窮也。夫小德以為之分，則富有之業足以見天地之全功；大德以為之本，則不貳之眞
translation_en:
Tong Chengqi

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The explanation of virtue in its lesser and greater aspects is exceptionally clear. This is precisely the subtle operation of creation and transformation, showing how the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Writers in the examination hall generally explain lesser and greater virtue in terms of substance and function. This essay alone grasps the intended meaning.

The Doctrine of the Mean investigates what makes creation and transformation great in order to reveal the greatness of the sage. The greatness of Heaven and Earth lies in their virtue. Without virtue, they would all but cease: how, then, could they be great? By considering this, we can understand the sage. Chapter Thirty of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven. Its meaning is, broadly, this: comparing Zhongni [Confucius] to Heaven and Earth means attributing to him their greatness. Yet where should we seek this greatness in Heaven and Earth themselves? Thus, between Heaven above, which covers, and Earth below, which supports, things do not harm one another, and their ways do not conflict. The reason is simply that lesser virtue flows like rivers. Responding to primordial transformation, things contract and expand, their diverse manifestations taking perceptible form; borne by the dynamic workings of vital energy, they emerge and withdraw, their onward movement following regular patterns. It is like the flow of rivers: their courses are clearly distinguished, and they proceed without ceasing. Things indeed develop together, and their ways proceed together. The reason is simply that greater virtue brings forth transformation in abundance. Yin and yang abide in their dwelling, with their intermingling constituting its operation; the Supreme Ultimate unifies the whole, with closing and opening constituting its pivot. Transformation is thus made abundant: its root is vast, and what issues from it is inexhaustible. Lesser virtue supplies its differentiated manifestations, so that the work of rich abundance suffices to reveal the full achievement of Heaven and Earth; greater virtue supplies its foundation, so that the reality of its undivided constancy …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
足以立天地之貞觀廣大之生觀諸其道而所
謂高明博厚者可識矣易簡之示求諸其德而
所謂覆載生成者不偏矣非天地之所以爲大
乎自聖人言之物各付物其小德之川流乎純
亦不已其大德之敦化乎聖人與天地合德於
是知仲尼之所以大矣夫子告曾子曰吾道一
以貫之夫貫者小德也一者大德也一以貫之
而聖人之德無餘蘊矣子思子作中庸語夫子
之德而譬之以天地之所以大其固受之曾子
===
而曾子唯之夫子者乎
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也詩云周道如砥其直如矢君子
所履小人所視
王宗道
同考試官教諭張 批 君子所守處點斷數語便
可見孟子自任微意
同考試官教諭鄭 批 孟子學有據守此類可見
考試官教諭黃 批 〔明切〕
punctuated:
足以立天地之貞觀。廣大之生，觀諸其道，而所謂高明博厚者可識矣；易簡之示，求諸其德，而所謂覆載生成者不偏矣。非天地之所以爲大乎？自聖人言之，物各付物，其小德之川流乎？純亦不已，其大德之敦化乎？聖人與天地合德，於是知仲尼之所以大矣。夫子告曾子曰：「吾道一以貫之。」夫貫者，小德也；一者，大德也。一以貫之，而聖人之德無餘蘊矣。子思子作《中庸》，語夫子之德，而譬之以天地之所以大，其固受之曾子，而曾子唯之夫子者乎？
夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。《詩》云：「周道如砥，其直如矢。君子所履，小人所視。」
王宗道
同考試官教諭張批：君子所守處，點斷數語，便可見孟子自任微意。
同考試官教諭鄭批：孟子學有據守，此類可見。
考試官教諭黃批：〔明切〕
translation_en:
…suffices to establish the constant pattern of Heaven and Earth. Observe their vast work of giving life in their Way, and what is meant by their loftiness, brilliance, breadth, and depth can be understood. Seek their manifestation of ease and simplicity in their virtue, and their work of sheltering, supporting, generating, and completing things proves impartial. Is this not what makes Heaven and Earth great? Speaking of the sage: assigning each thing its proper place—is this not his lesser virtue flowing like streams? Remaining pure and never ceasing—is this not his greater virtue abundantly transforming things? The sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth; from this we understand what makes Zhongni great. The Master told Zengzi, “My Way has one principle that runs through it.” What runs through the particulars is the lesser virtue; the one principle is the greater virtue. With one principle running through all, nothing of the sage’s virtue remains undisclosed. Master Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean, speaking of the Master’s virtue and comparing it to what makes Heaven and Earth great. Surely this was what he received from Zengzi, and what Zengzi affirmed with his assent to the Master?

“Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the gentleman can follow this road and enter and leave through this gate. The Book of Odes says: ‘The road of Zhou is like a whetstone, straight as an arrow. It is what the gentleman treads and what the common people look to.’”

Wang Zongdao.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “A few decisive words identifying what the gentleman holds fast to suffice to reveal the subtle meaning of Mengzi’s sense of his own responsibility.”

Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “That Mengzi’s learning had firm grounds to which he held fast can be seen in passages of this kind.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and pertinent.〕

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授陳批質確
大賢論道必體於君子而徵諸詩焉夫禮義所
以立人之道也惟君子爲能體之徵諸詩而益
信矣孟子之論如此且人君欲見賢而召之固
不以其道矣孰知賢者之自處有道乎夫道有
義焉行之而宜焉者是已義辟則路也道有禮
焉履之而理焉者是已禮辟則門也是道也人
皆有之而未必知務也惟君子也問學而閑之
於素厲行而守之於爲故行必以義也而非義
===
則弗行或往或來坦然是路之率由矣動必以
禮也而非禮則弗動一闔一闢允乎是門之出
入矣舍此而輕身以往見是無義也失己以干
進是無禮也無義無禮而君子豈爲之哉且詩
不云乎周道如砥其直如矢君子所履小人所
視夫如砥如矢可以見義路矣所履所視可以
見君子之能由矣能由是路則其出入是門者
可推已君子之自守如此爲人君者顧欲見而
召之可乎抑君子之在天下未嘗不欲有爲於
punctuated:
考試官教授陳批：質確。

大賢論道，必體於君子而徵諸詩焉。夫禮義所以立人之道也，惟君子爲能體之，徵諸詩而益信矣。孟子之論如此。且人君欲見賢而召之，固不以其道矣，孰知賢者之自處有道乎？夫道有義焉，行之而宜焉者是已。義辟則路也。道有禮焉，履之而理焉者是已。禮辟則門也。是道也，人皆有之，而未必知務也。惟君子也，問學而閑之於素，厲行而守之於爲，故行必以義也，而非義則弗行。或往或來，坦然是路之率由矣。動必以禮也，而非禮則弗動。一闔一闢，允乎是門之出入矣。舍此而輕身以往見，是無義也；失己以干進，是無禮也。無義無禮，而君子豈爲之哉？且詩不云乎：「周道如砥，其直如矢。君子所履，小人所視。」夫如砥如矢，可以見義路矣；所履所視，可以見君子之能由矣。能由是路，則其出入是門者可推已。君子之自守如此，爲人君者顧欲見而召之，可乎？抑君子之在天下，未嘗不欲有爲於
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Substantial and sound.”

When a great worthy discusses the Way, he necessarily considers its embodiment in the gentleman and seeks confirmation in the Book of Odes. Ritual propriety and righteousness establish the Way of being human. Only the gentleman can embody them; confirmation from the Odes makes this all the more certain. Such is Mencius’s argument. Now, when a ruler wishes to see a worthy man and summons him, he is plainly not proceeding according to the proper Way. Does he realize that the worthy man has a Way governing his own conduct?

The Way includes righteousness: this means acting as is fitting. By analogy, righteousness is a road. The Way includes ritual propriety: this means conducting oneself in accordance with principle. By analogy, ritual propriety is a gate. Everyone possesses this Way, yet not everyone knows to devote himself to it. Only the gentleman safeguards it through inquiry and learning in his everyday life, and upholds it in practice through strenuous effort. Thus his conduct must accord with righteousness; what is not righteous he will not do. Whether going or coming, he follows this broad, level road. His movements must accord with ritual propriety; where propriety is lacking, he will not move. With every closing and opening, he truly passes out and in through this gate. To abandon this and demean himself by going to seek an audience would be to lack righteousness; to compromise himself in pursuit of advancement would be to lack ritual propriety. How could a gentleman act without righteousness or propriety?

Moreover, do not the Odes say: “The road of Zhou is like a whetstone, straight as an arrow. It is what the gentleman treads, what the petty man looks upon”? Its being like a whetstone and like an arrow reveals righteousness as a road. Its being trodden and looked upon reveals the gentleman’s ability to follow it. If he can follow this road, we may infer that he also passes out and in through this gate. Such is the gentleman’s steadfast adherence to his principles. Can a ruler nevertheless summon him merely because he wishes to see him? Yet the gentleman, living in the world, has never been without the desire to accomplish something in …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天德在人雖无不備而能行之者鮮矣非君子
之至健其孰能與於此乾之辭曰元亨利貞夫
子既作彖傳以釋之矣而此又盡其蘊也今夫
乾者天也元亨利貞者其德也是德也豈獨專
於天乎故元者人之仁也貫乎萬善而為善之
長焉亨者人之禮也萃乎眾美而為嘉之會焉
利者義也義嚴於分而和所由生不曰義之和
乎貞者智也智明於理而事依以立不曰事之
幹乎是故人之所同得也而行之者其唯君子
===
乎故體仁以達愛也而足以長人嘉會以立敬
也而足以合禮隨物而使之宜則不乖於義而
義和知正而守之固則不昧於事而事立夫體
仁合禮則元亨之德行矣義和貞固則利貞之
德行矣然其所以能行此者何哉亦以其健耳
故曰乾元亨利貞言乾唯健故能行此四德君
子之健不異於天而豈不能行哉天人合一之
道於此見矣抑論之乾者健而无息之謂也天
非健則造化之功或幾於息矣君子法天以自
punctuated: 天德在人，雖无不備，而能行之者鮮矣。非君子之至健，其孰能與於此？乾之辭曰：「元亨利貞。」夫子既作彖傳以釋之矣，而此又盡其蘊也。今夫乾者，天也；元亨利貞者，其德也。是德也，豈獨專於天乎？故元者，人之仁也，貫乎萬善而為善之長焉；亨者，人之禮也，萃乎眾美而為嘉之會焉；利者，義也，義嚴於分而和所由生，不曰義之和乎？貞者，智也，智明於理而事依以立，不曰事之幹乎？是故人之所同得也，而行之者，其唯君子乎？故體仁以達愛也，而足以長人；嘉會以立敬也，而足以合禮；隨物而使之宜，則不乖於義而義和；知正而守之固，則不昧於事而事立。夫體仁合禮，則元亨之德行矣；義和貞固，則利貞之德行矣。然其所以能行此者何哉？亦以其健耳。故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」言乾唯健，故能行此四德。君子之健不異於天，而豈不能行哉？天人合一之道，於此見矣。抑論之，乾者，健而无息之謂也。天非健，則造化之功或幾於息矣。君子法天以自
translation_en: …although Heaven’s virtues are all fully present in human beings, few can put them into practice. Who could attain this without the gentleman’s utmost vigor? The statement for Qian reads, “Origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” The Master already composed the Commentary on the Judgments to explain it, but here he further brings out its full implications. Now, Qian is Heaven; origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy are its virtues. Could these virtues belong exclusively to Heaven? Thus origination is human benevolence: it runs through all goodness and is the chief of good qualities. Flourishing is human ritual propriety: it gathers together all excellences and is the convergence of what is fine. Benefit is righteousness: righteousness strictly distinguishes proper shares, and harmony arises from it. Is this not called “the harmony of righteousness”? Constancy is wisdom: wisdom clearly apprehends principle, and affairs depend upon it for their establishment. Is this not called “the backbone of affairs”? These, then, are what all people alike receive; yet is it not the gentleman alone who puts them into practice? Thus, by embodying benevolence and extending love, he is able to lead others; by bringing together what is fine and establishing reverence, he is able to accord with ritual propriety. By responding to things and ensuring that each receives what is fitting, he does not depart from righteousness, and righteousness is harmonious. By knowing what is correct and holding firmly to it, he is not benighted in affairs, and affairs are established. When he embodies benevolence and accords with ritual propriety, the virtues of origination and flourishing are put into practice; when righteousness is harmonious and constancy firm, the virtues of benefit and constancy are put into practice. But what enables him to practice these? It is simply his vigor. Hence the text says, “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” This means that Qian can enact these four virtues precisely because it is vigorous. The gentleman’s vigor does not differ from Heaven’s: how, then, could he fail to enact them? Here we see the Way by which Heaven and humanity form a unity. To consider it further, Qian means being vigorous without cessation. Were Heaven not vigorous, the work of creation and transformation might almost cease. The gentleman takes Heaven as his model in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
泰也與民均休戚而不拂其情知安享之非榮
也與民同好惡而不專其利由是至仁之恩涵
濡乎人心盛德之光敷賁乎遠邇被其澤者咸
切父母之依所欲在此而不能外也仰其休者
皆興皇王之戴其機甚速而不可禦也夫唯同
人如此而後治成於无外是固大有之義矣其
受之以大有者不有見於是乎大有之後而次
之以謙者又何也誠以大有之時治已極矣則
驕心易萌而不知治亂之相倚民已安矣則侈
===
心易肆而不知去留之靡常殆必凝承天命而
切兢業之懷顧畏民碞而謹怠荒之戒一日二
日有萬幾焉吾其敢以自逸耶匹夫匹婦或勝
予焉吾其可以自矜耶夫唯能謙如此而後治
保於无虞是固謙之義矣其受之以謙者不有
見於是乎吁觀於此義而人君制治保邦之道
具見之矣此序卦聖人所以深致意也歟稽古
人君克盡是道者其堯舜乎故黎民於變矣猶
勤欽若之思四方風動矣猶嚴逸遊之警此其
punctuated: 泰也，與民均休戚而不拂其情；知安享之非榮也，與民同好惡而不專其利。由是至仁之恩涵濡乎人心，盛德之光敷賁乎遠邇。被其澤者咸切父母之依，所欲在此而不能外也；仰其休者皆興皇王之戴，其機甚速而不可禦也。夫唯同人如此，而後治成於无外，是固大有之義矣。其受之以大有者，不有見於是乎？大有之後而次之以謙者，又何也？誠以大有之時，治已極矣，則驕心易萌，而不知治亂之相倚；民已安矣，則侈心易肆，而不知去留之靡常。殆必凝承天命而切兢業之懷，顧畏民碞而謹怠荒之戒。一日二日有萬幾焉，吾其敢以自逸耶？匹夫匹婦或勝予焉，吾其可以自矜耶？夫唯能謙如此，而後治保於无虞，是固謙之義矣。其受之以謙者，不有見於是乎？吁！觀於此義，而人君制治保邦之道具見之矣。此序卦聖人所以深致意也歟！稽古人君克盡是道者，其堯舜乎？故黎民於變矣，猶勤欽若之思；四方風動矣，猶嚴逸遊之警。此其
translation_en:
…ease, and shares the people's joys and sorrows without thwarting their feelings; he knows that enjoying comfort is no glory, and shares the people's likes and dislikes without monopolizing benefits. Thus the benevolence of his consummate humanity permeates people's hearts, and the radiance of his abundant virtue adorns places far and near. All who receive his bounty feel a deep attachment to him as to a parent: their desires center upon him and cannot turn elsewhere. All who look up to his beneficence come to support him as their sovereign; this impulse arises swiftly and cannot be checked. Only through Fellowship with Others (Tongren) of this kind can good government extend everywhere without exception. This is precisely the meaning of Great Possession (Dayou). Does not placing Great Possession after it reflect this understanding?

Why, then, does Modesty (Qian) follow Great Possession? Indeed, in a time of Great Possession, good government has already reached its height, so arrogance readily sprouts, and the ruler fails to recognize how order and disorder depend upon each other. The people are already at peace, so extravagance readily runs unchecked, and he fails to recognize how inconstantly they may leave or remain. He must surely receive Heaven's mandate with solemn reverence and cherish a vigilant, conscientious disposition; he must heed and fear the peril posed by the people, carefully observing the warning against negligence and dissipation. ‘In a single day or two there are ten thousand affairs requiring attention: dare I indulge in ease? An ordinary man or woman may surpass me: may I presume to be proud?’ Only with modesty of this kind can good government be preserved free from danger. This is precisely the meaning of Modesty. Does not placing Modesty after it reflect this understanding?

Ah! In considering this meaning, we see fully the ruler's way of establishing good government and preserving the realm. Is this not why the sage devoted such profound attention to the Sequence of the Hexagrams? Looking back to antiquity, were not Yao and Shun the rulers who fully realized this way? Thus, even when the common people had been transformed, they still diligently pondered how reverently to accord with Heaven; even when the four quarters responded as grass bends before the wind, they still strictly heeded warnings against idle pleasure. This was their…

遺迹而庶幾湯孫之不愧矣夫於是則知傳說
之言底可績而高宗之志大有爲也交責相懋
不以近功相徇此所以稱盛治而不衰也歟抑
考知行之說傅說始發之遂爲萬世學問之要
然知行竝者也而曰知易行難者何蓋因高宗
舊學之力而進之以行也若夫爲學君子則當
自致知始而以行副之從事於遜志時敏之訓
punctuated: 是者。蓋爲治之道，不貴於徒言，而納諫之誠，當推諸實踐。得於耳者，不若體之之切；樂於聞者，恒苦於行之之難也。夫行之所以難者，由信之不篤耳。王如明以致察，而信臣言之必可行；健以致决，而信吾力之必可任，則志至氣從，而措其知於允蹈；說繹從改，而尊所聞於高明，則亦不爲難矣。誠如是，則所以繼述先王者，不在玆耶？夫先王之成德遠矣，而王今日則允協之。能靈於承，所以彰其啟佑者益至；有爲之後，所以傳其盛美者無窮。修身用人之懿，率烈祖攸行，而粲然殷道之復興矣；治民事神之休，迪高后遺迹，而庶幾湯孫之不愧矣。夫於是則知傳說之言底可績，而高宗之志大有爲也。交責相懋，不以近功相徇，此所以稱盛治而不衰也歟！抑考知行之說，傅說始發之，遂爲萬世學問之要。然知行竝者也，而曰知易行難者何？蓋因高宗舊學之力，而進之以行也。若夫爲學君子，則當自致知始，而以行副之，從事於遜志時敏之訓
translation_en:
…beyond this. For the way of governing does not prize mere words: sincerity in accepting remonstrance must be extended into practice. What one receives through the ears is less immediate than what one embodies oneself; what one delights in hearing often proves difficult to carry out. The difficulty of acting arises simply from insufficiently firm conviction. If Your Majesty exercises discernment to examine matters thoroughly, trusting that your servant’s words can indeed be put into practice, and exercises strength to reach a decision, trusting that your own powers can indeed bear the task, then, wherever your resolve reaches, your vital energies will follow, and you will put your knowledge faithfully into practice. Through explanation, compliance, and reform [?], you will raise what you have heard to a lofty and enlightened plane; this, too, will cease to be difficult. If this is truly so, does not the means of continuing and fulfilling the work of the former kings lie here?

The perfected virtue of the former kings lies far in the past, yet Your Majesty today can truly accord with it. By ably and perceptively carrying on their legacy [?], you will manifest ever more fully the guidance and protection they bestowed. With an accomplished successor, the transmission of their splendid achievements will have no end. In the excellence of cultivating yourself and employing others, you will follow the illustrious ancestors’ conduct, and the way of Yin will flourish anew in all its brilliance. In the goodness of governing the people and serving the spirits, you will follow the traces left by the exalted sovereigns, and may thus prove worthy of being Tang’s descendant.

From this we see that Fu Yue’s words could indeed bring tangible results, and that Gaozong’s resolve promised great accomplishments. They held one another to account and encouraged one another, neither accommodating the other for the sake of immediate achievements. Is this not why their rule was acclaimed as flourishing and did not decline? Moreover, examining the teaching concerning knowledge and action, we find that Fu Yue first articulated it, and it consequently became an essential principle of learning for all ages. Yet knowledge and action go together: why, then, did he say that knowing is easy and acting difficult? It was because he built upon the strength of Gaozong’s previous learning and urged him onward to action. As for gentlemen pursuing learning, they should begin by extending their knowledge, match it with action, and apply themselves to the injunction to be humble in purpose and constantly diligent …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則幾矣然則說命一書雖當時告君之言實心
學之元經也
以佑乃辟永康兆民萬邦惟無斁
王喬衡
同考試官教諭潘批〔能究輔君以安民之旨〕
同考試官教授林批〔萬邦無斁處能言安民之效〕
考試官教諭黃批〔成王命官意正如此〕
考試官教授陳批〔精切〕
賢王勉羣臣輔君以安民而得天下之心也夫
===
君道莫要於安民也輔之以修職之羣臣其得
天下之心宜矣成王訓迪百官於篇終而申敕
之曰玆欲爾三事曁大夫敬官以治政者豈有
他哉亦惟曰安民而已夫安民之責君實主之
而臣則輔之者也爾其夙夜匪懈同乃心以匡
吾智力之所不及左右有方修乃職以助吾心
思之所欲爲使政治益明而萬物各得其所惠
鮮懷保之仁可永傳而勿替也教化大洽而一
夫無有不獲燮和時敘之澤可敷錫于無窮也
punctuated:
則幾矣。然則《說命》一書，雖當時告君之言，實心學之元經也。
以佑乃辟，永康兆民，萬邦惟無斁。
王喬衡
同考試官教諭潘批〔能究輔君以安民之旨〕
同考試官教授林批〔萬邦無斁處能言安民之效〕
考試官教諭黃批〔成王命官意正如此〕
考試官教授陳批〔精切〕
賢王勉羣臣輔君以安民，而得天下之心也。夫君道莫要於安民也，輔之以修職之羣臣，其得天下之心宜矣。成王訓迪百官，於篇終而申敕之曰：「玆欲爾三事曁大夫敬官以治政者，豈有他哉？亦惟曰安民而已。夫安民之責，君實主之，而臣則輔之者也。爾其夙夜匪懈，同乃心以匡吾智力之所不及，左右有方，修乃職以助吾心思之所欲爲，使政治益明，而萬物各得其所。惠鮮懷保之仁，可永傳而勿替也；教化大洽，而一夫無有不獲，燮和時敘之澤，可敷錫于無窮也。
translation_en:
…then one would come close. Thus the Charge to Yue (Yue ming), though spoken to instruct a ruler at that time, is in truth a foundational classic of the learning of the mind.

“Assist your sovereign, secure lasting peace for the myriad people, and let the myriad states never grow weary.”

Wang Qiaoheng

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “Successfully explores the purport of assisting the ruler to bring peace to the people.”
Associate Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “In treating ‘the myriad states never grow weary,’ successfully explains the effects of bringing peace to the people.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Precisely such was King Cheng’s intent in charging his officials.”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Refined and incisive.”

The worthy king exhorts his ministers to assist their ruler in bringing peace to the people and thereby winning the hearts of all under Heaven. Nothing is more essential to the way of rulership than bringing peace to the people. Assisted by ministers who discharge their duties, the ruler should indeed win the hearts of all under Heaven. Having instructed the hundred officials, King Cheng reiterates his admonition at the chapter’s end, saying: “In desiring you, the Three Dukes and the grand masters, to attend reverently to your offices and conduct government, could I have any other purpose? It is simply to bring peace to the people. The ruler bears the chief responsibility for bringing peace to the people, while his ministers assist him. Be unremitting morning and night; unite your hearts to remedy what my wisdom and strength cannot accomplish. Assist me with proper methods and discharge your duties to help accomplish what my mind intends. Thus let government become ever more enlightened and all things find their proper place. The benevolence that succors the distressed, cherishes the people, and protects them may then endure forever without decline. Moral instruction will spread everywhere, leaving not a single person without their due, and the blessings of harmony and timely order may be bestowed without end. …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是故萬邦者兆民之所止也民安則邦孚矣曰
采曰流雖遠於錯建而撫綏有道自盡得其歡
心異俗異齊雖不可強同而容保無疆自同歸
於大順大邦畏其力也小邦懷其德也其修和
有夏者猶其在於文祖矣遠之則有望也近之
則不厭也其媚玆一人者猶其在於烈考矣而
何有於厭斁者耶安民至是人臣事君之道始
無愧矣可不共圖之哉抑考成王之時四海攸
同六服承德而殷之頑民已友遜矣而猶汲汲
===
於安民何也蓋嘗求之皐陶之謨曰在知人在
安民夫知人安民雖若二事而知人其要也人
之弗知而求民之安者末矣故成王董正治官
知人之則而安民之寄也勞於求賢而逸於得
人乃可以長治若曰治安矣而般樂怠傲則復
隍之幾豈遠乎此成王之賢所以益基周歷也
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻爲此春酒以介眉壽七月食
punctuated:
是故，萬邦者，兆民之所止也。民安則邦孚矣。曰采曰流，雖遠於錯建，而撫綏有道，自盡得其歡心；異俗異齊，雖不可強同，而容保無疆，自同歸於大順。大邦畏其力也，小邦懷其德也，其修和有夏者，猶其在於文祖矣。遠之則有望也，近之則不厭也，其媚玆一人者，猶其在於烈考矣。而何有於厭斁者耶？安民至是，人臣事君之道始無愧矣，可不共圖之哉？抑考成王之時，四海攸同，六服承德，而殷之頑民已友遜矣，而猶汲汲於安民，何也？蓋嘗求之皐陶之謨，曰：「在知人，在安民。」夫知人、安民，雖若二事，而知人其要也。人之弗知而求民之安者，末矣。故成王董正治官，知人之則，而安民之寄也。勞於求賢，而逸於得人，乃可以長治。若曰治安矣，而般樂怠傲，則復隍之幾，豈遠乎？此成王之賢所以益基周歷也。

詩

六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剝棗，十月穫稻，爲此春酒，以介眉壽。七月食
translation_en:
Thus, the myriad states are where the teeming people dwell. When the people are at peace, the states are trustworthy. The Cai and Liu domains, though far away among the dispersed fiefs, will all give their wholehearted allegiance when comforted and pacified in the proper way. Their differing customs and practices cannot be forcibly made uniform; yet, through boundless tolerance and protection, all will come together in great concord. The great states fear his power, and the small states cherish his virtue. His cultivation of harmony throughout the lands of Xia will match that under his cultured ancestor. Those far away yearn for him, while those nearby never tire of him. Their love for this One Man will match that under his illustrious deceased father. How, then, could there be any weariness or aversion? Only when bringing peace to the people has reached this point can a minister be without shame in the way he serves his ruler. Can we fail to strive for this together?

Yet consider the time of King Cheng: all within the Four Seas were united, the six service zones acknowledged his virtue, and even the recalcitrant people of Yin had become friendly and compliant. Why, then, was he still so urgently concerned with bringing peace to the people? I have sought the answer in the Counsels of Gao Yao, which says: “It lies in knowing men; it lies in bringing peace to the people.” Although knowing men and bringing peace to the people seem to be two matters, knowing men is the essential one. To seek peace for the people without knowing men is to attend merely to the secondary. Thus, King Cheng’s supervision and rectification of the governing officials provided a standard for knowing men and entrusted them with bringing peace to the people. Only by exerting oneself in seeking the worthy, and then enjoying ease once the right men are found, can lasting good government be achieved. If one declares that order and peace have been secured and gives oneself over to pleasure, negligence, and arrogance, can the moment when the city wall collapses back into its moat be far off? This is how King Cheng’s worthiness further strengthened the foundations of Zhou’s enduring rule.

Book of Odes

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
瓜八月斷壺九月叔苴采荼薪樗食我
農夫
余賢
同考試官教諭張批是作從容而可深思
同考試官教諭鄭批文義有溫厚之味
考試官教諭黃批簡爭
考試官教授陳批朴雅
豳民因物以制用而致養之道備矣蓋豐於養
老而儉以自奉此豳俗異致其養者而其用不
===
匱矣乎周公述之以告成王如此蓋曰我豳風
俗之厚每於少長之節見之蓋其有敬德以尊
高年於是采四時之異而羞耇之儀行焉六月
而食鬱及薁也七月而亨葵及菽也八月則剝
棗焉十月則穫稻焉故以之為酒為醴畀我尸
賓稱觴登堂而眉壽介以無疆矣其於老者不
有餘敬哉有儉德以崇敦樸於是循日用之常
而逮下之義盡焉瓜之成於七月者可食也壺
之熟於八月者可斷也九月而叔苴於野焉采
punctuated:
瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴，采荼薪樗，食我農夫。
余賢。
同考試官教諭張批：是作從容而可深思。
同考試官教諭鄭批：文義有溫厚之味。
考試官教諭黃批：簡爭。
考試官教授陳批：朴雅。
豳民因物以制用，而致養之道備矣。蓋豐於養老，而儉以自奉，此豳俗異致其養者，而其用不匱矣乎？周公述之以告成王如此。蓋曰：我豳風俗之厚，每於少長之節見之。蓋其有敬德以尊高年，於是采四時之異，而羞耇之儀行焉。六月而食鬱及薁也，七月而亨葵及菽也，八月則剝棗焉，十月則穫稻焉。故以之為酒為醴，畀我尸賓，稱觴登堂，而眉壽介以無疆矣。其於老者，不有餘敬哉？有儉德以崇敦樸，於是循日用之常，而逮下之義盡焉。瓜之成於七月者可食也，壺之熟於八月者可斷也，九月而叔苴於野焉，采
translation_en:
…melons; in the eighth month, cut gourds; in the ninth month, gather hemp seed; gather bitter herbs and cut ailanthus for firewood, to feed our farmers.

Yu Xian.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “This composition is unhurried and invites deep reflection.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the composition has a gentle and generous quality.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Concise and forceful [?].”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Unadorned and elegant.”

The people of Bin regulated their consumption according to the resources available, and thus fully provided for nourishment. They were generous in supporting the elderly but frugal in providing for themselves. Was it not through this custom of Bin, which differentiated the provisions made for each group, that their resources never ran short? Such was the Duke of Zhou’s account when he instructed King Cheng. Its meaning was this: the generosity of our customs in Bin is always apparent in the distinctions observed between young and old. Possessing the virtue of reverence, the people honor those advanced in years. They therefore gather the special produce of the four seasons and carry out the rites of presenting food to the aged. In the sixth month they eat bush cherries and wild grapes; in the seventh, they boil mallows and beans; in the eighth, they knock down jujubes; and in the tenth, they harvest rice. With these they make wine and sweet liquor, presenting them to the personators of the ancestors and to guests. They ascend the hall and raise their cups, wishing the elders boundless longevity. Do they not show abundant reverence toward the aged?

Possessing the virtue of frugality, they esteem simplicity and plain living. They therefore follow the ordinary practices of daily sustenance and fully discharge their obligation to extend care to those below them. Melons that ripen in the seventh month may be eaten; gourds that mature in the eighth month may be cut; in the ninth month they gather hemp seed in the fields and gather…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
荼以茹而薪樗以爨焉故以之饁彼南畝食我
農人利用養生而數口可以無饑矣其於少者
不有餘愛哉夫豐儉有節則奢不得以敗制少
長有辨則瀆不得以敗倫觀豳之俗可以知民
德之厚哉抑周公陳無逸以告成王與七月一
詩相為表裏無非欲王知所以觀民即觀於農
圃飲食而民之勤儉孝敬之義炳焉夫雖民俗
之所自致而上之所以倡率者不可誣已故曰
觀於鄉而知王道之易易也
===
倬彼雲漢為章于天周王壽考遐不作人
李正彛
同考試官教諭張批聖化難言子能發之
同考試官教諭鄭批舂容能得雅義之盡
考試官教諭黃批醇雅
考試官教授陳批清潤
詩人即天之文以興聖人之化焉夫觀乎天文
而聖人之化可知矣自非文王久於其道其何
以與於斯故棫樸詩人歌文王之德曰仰觀於
punctuated:
荼以茹，而薪樗以爨焉，故以之饁彼南畝，食我農人，利用養生，而數口可以無饑矣。其於少者，不有餘愛哉？夫豐儉有節，則奢不得以敗制；少長有辨，則瀆不得以敗倫。觀豳之俗，可以知民德之厚哉！抑周公陳《無逸》以告成王，與《七月》一詩相為表裏，無非欲王知所以觀民，即觀於農圃飲食，而民之勤儉孝敬之義炳焉。夫雖民俗之所自致，而上之所以倡率者不可誣已。故曰：「觀於鄉，而知王道之易易也。」

倬彼雲漢，為章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人。
李正彛
同考試官教諭張批：「聖化難言，子能發之。」
同考試官教諭鄭批：「舂容，能得雅義之盡。」

考試官教授陳批：「清潤。」

translation_en:
…bitter herbs for food, and use the wood of the tree of heaven as fuel for cooking. With these they take meals to the southern fields and feed our farmers, making good use of resources to sustain life, so that a household of several mouths may be free from hunger. Is this not abundant love for the young? When abundance and frugality are properly regulated, extravagance cannot undermine established norms; when the distinctions between young and old are maintained, irreverence cannot undermine human relationships. By observing the customs of Bin, one can recognize the depth of the people’s virtue!

Moreover, the Duke of Zhou set forth “Against Idleness” to admonish King Cheng; it and the poem “Seventh Month” complement one another. Their sole purpose was to teach the king how to observe the people: simply by observing their farming, gardening, food, and drink, the principles of their diligence, frugality, filial devotion, and respect become manifest. Although these customs developed among the people themselves, the guidance and example provided by their rulers cannot be denied. Thus it is said: “By observing the village, one knows how very easy the kingly Way is to practice.”

“Brilliant is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in Heaven. The king of Zhou enjoys long life: how could he fail to nurture men of worth?”

Li Zhengyi.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The sage’s transforming influence is difficult to express, yet you have brought it forth.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Unhurried and ample, it fully captures the meaning of the Court Hymn.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Clear and polished.”

The poet draws upon the patterned beauty of Heaven to evoke the sage’s transforming influence. By observing Heaven’s patterns, one can understand the sage’s transforming influence.
