Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: 〔Concerned about the times and versed in adapting to change; clear in exposition and free of pedantry.〕

I have heard that one whose stipend amounts to no more than a few handfuls is in no position to speak of managing a household, and one whose stores do not fill a load or a shi-measure is in no position to plan affairs. You, honored examiners, discuss Chu’s tribute and taxes and seek counsel even from us students; I know I am inadequate to this task. Nevertheless, as a man of Chu, though I know nothing of what lies beyond Chu, I can still speak on its behalf. May I set out all the particulars before you?

Present-day Huguang is ancient Chu. Its land was formerly fertile but is now poor; its taxes were formerly heavy but are now light. Why is this? In ancient times, human labor fully exploited the land’s potential; today, land is plentiful but people are insufficient. A Han writer said of Jing and Yang: “They fell trees and plant grain, burn the scrub and sow millet, plow with fire and weed with water. The land is extensive and rich in resources; hence the people are indolent…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而偷生夫此蓋楚之遺也陵遲至於三國
則以荆州爲必爭故兵革所加致地薄而
民窮吳孫皓之所以徙都而失也休息至
於六朝則以武昌爲重鎮故人物所萃致
地沃而民剽唐崔郾之所以治鄂以嚴也
若宋與元則復瘠貧矣我
朝分服經野舉全楚地而爲之省居金陵之
上游抗東南之形勢非不重矣然承平既
久生齒日繁而不能使地之不爲瘠土人
===
之不爲下農何哉其地利猶未盡耳其賦
也蓋不必加於五等民猶以爲重也其貢
也蓋不必甲於九州民猶以爲難也是故
湖之稅糧以石計者二百十萬有奇耳而
貢賦徭役皆於是乎成之以漕于京謂之
兌運以輸于留都以餽于他省以制藩祿
以備邊儲謂之撥運以俸百官以廩弟子
員以餉守卒謂之存留其賦有如此者非
全力則匱而不支羽毛之類每歲上供有
punctuated: 而偷生。夫此蓋楚之遺也。陵遲至於三國，則以荆州爲必爭，故兵革所加，致地薄而民窮，吳孫皓之所以徙都而失也。休息至於六朝，則以武昌爲重鎮，故人物所萃，致地沃而民剽，唐崔郾之所以治鄂以嚴也。若宋與元，則復瘠貧矣。我朝分服經野，舉全楚地而爲之省，居金陵之上游，抗東南之形勢，非不重矣。然承平既久，生齒日繁，而不能使地之不爲瘠土、人之不爲下農，何哉？其地利猶未盡耳。其賦也，蓋不必加於五等，民猶以爲重也；其貢也，蓋不必甲於九州，民猶以爲難也。是故湖之稅糧，以石計者二百十萬有奇耳，而貢賦徭役皆於是乎成之。以漕于京，謂之兌運；以輸于留都，以餽于他省，以制藩祿，以備邊儲，謂之撥運；以俸百官，以廩弟子員，以餉守卒，謂之存留。其賦有如此者，非全力則匱而不支。羽毛之類，每歲上供有
translation_en:
…and merely eke out a living. This, indeed, is a legacy of Chu. As conditions deteriorated down to the Three Kingdoms period, Jingzhou became a place that rival powers had to contest. Warfare consequently impoverished the land and its people: this was why Sun Hao of Wu failed when he moved his capital there. With respite and recovery down through the Six Dynasties, Wuchang became a major stronghold. People and resources therefore gathered there, making the land fertile but the people fierce: this was why Cui Yan of the Tang governed Ezhou strictly. Under the Song and Yuan, however, the region again became barren and poor.

Our dynasty apportioned its jurisdictions and laid out its territories, taking the whole land of Chu and making it a province. Situated upstream from Jinling and commanding the strategic configuration of the southeast, it is certainly important. Yet, after a long period of peace, with the population increasing daily, why has it proved impossible to keep the land from being impoverished and the people from being poor farmers? It is simply that the land’s productive potential has still not been fully realized. Its tax assessment need not exceed the fifth grade, yet the people still consider it burdensome; its tribute need not rank first among the Nine Provinces, yet the people still find it difficult to supply.

Thus Huguang’s grain tax amounts to only a little over 2,100,000 shi, yet tribute, taxation, and labor-service obligations must all be met from this. Grain transported by water to the capital is called ‘grain transferred for shipment’ (duiyun). Grain sent to the secondary capital, supplied to other provinces, used to provide stipends for the imperial princes, or set aside for frontier reserves is called ‘allocated shipments’ (boyun). Grain used to pay officials, provide allowances for government students, and provision garrison soldiers is called ‘retained revenue’ (cunliu). Such are its tax obligations: unless the utmost effort is made, resources run short and cannot meet them. As for such items as feathers and hair, the annual supplies presented to the throne have…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
常數者爲歲辨丹漆之類因事而取無常
數者爲派辨蓋雖名殊於禹貢而實備乎
周官矣其貢有如此者非豫事則逋而不
前其餘泛應之需有身有田而取之者爲
丁糧雇役力役而征之者爲均徭其徭役
有如此者非多方濟之則偏而不舉就其
中而較之其有常數與雖無常數而義弗
獲已者無說也
宗藩之祿已似不敷矣而况於數十年後乎
===
請稍輕其折直而通融之則猶有數十年
之計也何也湖地藩祿之折支固重於他
所也過此非愚生所能知矣若江濟馬舩
之夫役
國初編之民間而用其人遂以爲戶至于今
戶絕業更而不可稽者多矣而猶責其雇
直而輸之夫編發猶謫戍也戍而絕者罷
勾而此之不罷何也請自今籍其戶存者
罷其戶絕者存而不願役者輸其直不繼
punctuated:
常數者爲歲辨，丹漆之類因事而取、無常數者爲派辨。蓋雖名殊於《禹貢》，而實備乎《周官》矣。其貢有如此者，非豫事則逋而不前。其餘泛應之需，有身有田而取之者爲丁糧，雇役力役而征之者爲均徭。其徭役有如此者，非多方濟之則偏而不舉。就其中而較之，其有常數與雖無常數而義弗獲已者，無說也。
宗藩之祿已似不敷矣，而况於數十年後乎？請稍輕其折直而通融之，則猶有數十年之計也。何也？湖地藩祿之折支固重於他所也。過此，非愚生所能知矣。
若江濟馬舩之夫役，國初編之民間而用其人，遂以爲戶。至于今，戶絕業更而不可稽者多矣，而猶責其雇直而輸之。夫編發猶謫戍也，戍而絕者罷勾，而此之不罷，何也？請自今籍其戶存者，罷其戶絕者；存而不願役者，輸其直；不繼
translation_en:
…those with fixed quotas are termed annual procurements. Items such as cinnabar and lacquer, obtained as occasions require and without fixed quotas, are termed apportioned procurements. Although their names differ from those in the Tribute of Yu, their substance is fully covered in the Offices of Zhou. Such are the tribute obligations: unless preparations are made beforehand, deliveries fall into arrears and fail to proceed. Of the remaining miscellaneous requirements, levies assessed on persons and land are termed poll and grain levies; those exacted through hired service or personal labor are termed equalized labor service. Such are the labor-service obligations: unless provision is made in various ways, the burden falls unevenly and the services cannot be carried out. Comparing these obligations, there is nothing to be said against those with fixed quotas, or those which, though lacking fixed quotas, cannot rightfully be avoided.
The stipends of the imperial princes already seem inadequately funded; how much worse will matters be several decades hence! I ask that their commuted monetary value be reduced somewhat and adjustments made, so that there may still be a workable arrangement for several decades. Why? Because the commuted payments for princely stipends in Huguang are indeed heavier than elsewhere. Beyond this, I, an ignorant student, cannot say.
As for the labor service for the river-crossing horse boats [?], at the founding of the dynasty men were enrolled from among the common people and put to work, and their households were consequently registered for this service. By now, many such households have died out or their property has changed hands, making them impossible to trace; yet payment of the cost of hiring substitutes is still demanded. Assignment to such service is like banishment to frontier garrison duty. When a household liable for garrison service dies out, the requisitioning of replacements ceases; why does it not cease in this case? I ask that, henceforth, surviving households be registered and extinct households be released from the obligation. Those that survive but are unwilling to perform the service should pay its monetary equivalent; if they fail to continue…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則充發而洊補焉亦庶乎其可也舍此非
愚生所能知矣雖然此猶未及其大也楚
自比年以來官無藏矣大木之役既括而
盈其資苗夷之役又舉而爲之餉皆未厎
其數也屬者督逋之部使相尋而至楚民
雖有一熟之力何以堪之宋人有破分之
法既及分則諸司住催版曹不問由是州
縣得其贏餘以相補助貧民亦得遷延以
待放蠲此不可行之今也乎雖然此猶未
===
及其甚難也比年以來
聖恩肆眚則有免恤災則有免免者無從出矣
而又不可不舉其全數以爲用則有多方
區畫補助而已姑以十年之事槩之癸甲
而後以迄于今則聞計補四百餘萬矣積
儲有限經費無窮不曰甚難矣乎則夫贓
罰徒贖之調取吾固知當事者之疲於奔
命也矣夫
聖天子軫念湯沐不忍其供應之煩工役之勞
punctuated: 則充發而洊補焉，亦庶乎其可也。舍此，非愚生所能知矣。雖然，此猶未及其大也。楚自比年以來，官無藏矣。大木之役，既括而盈其資；苗夷之役，又舉而爲之餉，皆未厎其數也。屬者，督逋之部使相尋而至，楚民雖有一熟之力，何以堪之？宋人有破分之法，既及分，則諸司住催，版曹不問。由是州縣得其贏餘以相補助，貧民亦得遷延以待放蠲。此不可行之今也乎？雖然，此猶未及其甚難也。比年以來，聖恩肆眚則有免，恤災則有免。免者無從出矣，而又不可不舉其全數以爲用，則有多方區畫補助而已。姑以十年之事槩之，癸甲而後，以迄于今，則聞計補四百餘萬矣。積儲有限，經費無窮，不曰甚難矣乎？則夫贓罰徒贖之調取，吾固知當事者之疲於奔命也矣。夫聖天子軫念湯沐，不忍其供應之煩、工役之勞
translation_en:
…then men should be assigned and dispatched to replenish the service ranks in succession; this too might prove practicable. Beyond this, your humble student knows no solution. Yet this still does not touch upon the larger problem. In recent years, the government treasuries of Chu have been emptied. For the large-timber procurement service, resources have already been collected exhaustively to provide its funding; for the campaign against the Miao peoples, funds have again been raised for military provisions. Neither has yet reached the required amount. Recently, ministry envoys charged with collecting arrears have arrived one after another. Even with the resources afforded by one good harvest, how can the people of Chu bear this? Under the Song there was a system of fractional collection (pofen): once the prescribed fraction had been reached, the various offices ceased pressing for payment, and the Ministry of Revenue made no further inquiry. Thus prefectures and counties could use their surpluses to assist one another, while poor people could gain time and await remission. Could this not be implemented today?

Yet this still does not touch upon the gravest difficulty. In recent years, imperial acts of grace granting general amnesties have brought remissions, as has relief for disasters. There is no source from which to obtain the sums remitted, yet the full amount must still be raised to meet expenditure. Officials can only devise various means of making up the shortfall. Taking roughly the affairs of the past ten years, I have heard that, from the gui and jia years down to the present, the supplements have totaled more than four million [units unspecified]. Reserves are finite, while regular expenses have no end. Can this not be called an extreme difficulty? As for requisitioning confiscated illicit gains, fines, and payments redeeming penal servitude, I well understand how those responsible have exhausted themselves rushing to comply with orders. The sagely Son of Heaven cherishes his ancestral domain and cannot bear the burdens of its provisioning obligations or the toil of its labor services…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也而屢免其租爲守土之臣者正宜將順
德美而亦焉忍使
帝鄕之民不獲樂樂利利以謳歌太平而已耶
此固忠愛者之所當念而惕也愚聞之竭
澤而漁魚焉再得矣反裘而負薪毛安所
傅矣執事亦知楚之民乎人無世業易以
委棄也糧無定額田已鬻而籍猶存也不
能貿遷有無轉移執事無以助耕之不及
也樹藝無法起土播種一舉而聽于天時
===
也家鮮蓋藏有急則舉其食以易金而輸
之官所謂穀太賤則傷農也濱江之區水
暴漲則思免魚高仰之地陂塘之不講而
灌漑之無策則水旱之患無歲無之也此
六者楚之所以瘠而貧也若今年江漢皆
溢決隄防漂田廬流離盜竊之不免則又
甚矣爲今之計急務莫先於議賑實惠莫
大於緩征永功莫重於興水利常法莫美
於修常平要機莫宜於課有司大本莫過
punctuated:
也，而屢免其租。爲守土之臣者，正宜將順德美，而亦焉忍使帝鄕之民不獲樂樂利利，以謳歌太平而已耶？此固忠愛者之所當念而惕也。愚聞之：竭澤而漁，魚焉再得矣？反裘而負薪，毛安所傅矣？執事亦知楚之民乎？人無世業，易以委棄也；糧無定額，田已鬻而籍猶存也；不能貿遷有無，轉移執事，無以助耕之不及也；樹藝無法，起土播種，一舉而聽于天時也；家鮮蓋藏，有急則舉其食以易金而輸之官，所謂穀太賤則傷農也；濱江之區，水暴漲則思免魚，高仰之地，陂塘之不講而灌漑之無策，則水旱之患無歲無之也。此六者，楚之所以瘠而貧也。若今年江漢皆溢，決隄防，漂田廬，流離盜竊之不免，則又甚矣。
爲今之計，急務莫先於議賑，實惠莫大於緩征，永功莫重於興水利，常法莫美於修常平，要機莫宜於課有司，大本莫過
translation_en:
…and has repeatedly remitted their land tax. Ministers charged with governing this territory should surely support and carry forward his virtuous intentions. How could they bear to let the people of the imperial homeland be denied the enjoyment of their pleasures and benefits, and the opportunity to sing the praises of peaceful rule? This is certainly something that those devoted to their sovereign and concerned for the people should ponder with vigilance. I have heard it said: if you drain a marsh to catch fish, how will you obtain fish again? If you turn a fur coat inside out to carry firewood, to what will its fur remain attached?
Do you, sir, also understand the people of Chu? They have no settled hereditary livelihoods and readily abandon what they have. Their grain-tax assessments are not fixed: even after their fields have been sold, the holdings remain registered under their names. They cannot trade goods to exchange what they have for what they lack, or shift to other occupations [?], and thus have no means of supplementing what farming fails to provide. Their cultivation lacks method: they turn the soil and sow, then leave everything to the weather. Few households have reserves; when an urgent need arises, they sell their food for money to remit to the authorities. This is what is meant by saying that excessively cheap grain harms farmers. In districts along the river, when the waters suddenly rise, people think only of escaping a watery death. On higher ground, ponds and reservoirs receive no attention, and there is no plan for irrigation. Thus not a year passes without damage from flood or drought. These six conditions explain why Chu is impoverished. This year, moreover, both the Yangzi and the Han have overflowed, breaching embankments and sweeping away fields and homes. Displacement and theft have inevitably followed, making matters still worse.
In planning for the present, no urgent task takes precedence over deliberating on relief; no tangible benefit exceeds postponing tax collection; no lasting achievement matters more than developing water management; no standing measure is better than restoring the ever-normal granary system; no essential means is more appropriate than assessing the responsible officials; and no fundamental undertaking surpasses…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於清田賦議賑之說於被災之處悉委之
有司使人自爲法而稽其成勞賦卹有虛
者罪之可也若繩以文法待以歲月則不
及矣緩征之說先蠲積逋次減見供可也
不然緩之則爲姦吏之所蠶食急之則爲
盜賊之所憑藉矣水利之說昔人有云善
爲溝者水必漱齧之而無所壅以其因水
勢故也善爲防者水必淫液之而無所決
以其因地勢故也即今俟水涸而修壞防
===
宜勿惜小費而堅厚之是務若陂塘則不
可不講矣然豈能易因勢之論哉修常平
則昔人有云其弊有四一曰掌倉之弊二
曰點檢之弊三曰出貸之弊四曰回收之
弊今之預備倉之弊實類此擇人以任之
則去此四弊矣而愚以爲有糶糴而無斂
散可也夫富民之寄莫先於有司矣長吏
以墾田爲課最佐吏以勸農爲職業不取
其矯飾外貌而取其悃愊無華不貴其繭
punctuated: 於清田賦。議賑之說，於被災之處悉委之有司，使人自爲法而稽其成勞，賦卹有虛者罪之，可也。若繩以文法，待以歲月，則不及矣。緩征之說，先蠲積逋，次減見供，可也。不然，緩之則爲姦吏之所蠶食，急之則爲盜賊之所憑藉矣。水利之說，昔人有云：「善爲溝者，水必漱齧之而無所壅，以其因水勢故也；善爲防者，水必淫液之而無所決，以其因地勢故也。」即今俟水涸而修壞防，宜勿惜小費，而堅厚之是務。若陂塘，則不可不講矣。然豈能易因勢之論哉？修常平，則昔人有云：「其弊有四：一曰掌倉之弊，二曰點檢之弊，三曰出貸之弊，四曰回收之弊。」今之預備倉之弊實類此，擇人以任之，則去此四弊矣。而愚以爲有糶糴而無斂散，可也。夫富民之寄，莫先於有司矣。長吏以墾田爲課最，佐吏以勸農爲職業，不取其矯飾外貌，而取其悃愊無華，不貴其繭
translation_en:
…than putting the land tax in order. As for deliberating on famine relief, responsibility in the afflicted areas may be entrusted entirely to the local officials, allowing each to devise measures and then examining their accomplishments; those whose distribution of relief involves false claims should be punished. If instead they are bound by administrative formalities and made to wait months and years, relief will come too late. As for deferring tax collection, accumulated arrears should first be remitted, and current obligations then reduced. Otherwise, deferred collections will be eaten away by corrupt clerks, while pressing for payment will give bandits an opportunity to exploit.

As for water management, someone of old said: “When channels are well constructed, the water scours and erodes them without becoming obstructed, because they follow the flow of the water. When embankments are well constructed, water seeps through them without breaching them, because they follow the configuration of the land.” Now, when the waters have subsided and damaged embankments are repaired, one should not begrudge small expenditures, but concentrate on making them solid and thick. Reservoirs and ponds, too, must receive attention. Yet how could one depart from this principle of following the natural configuration?

As for restoring the Ever-Normal Granaries, someone of old said: “There are four abuses: first, abuses in managing the granaries; second, abuses in inspection; third, abuses in making loans; fourth, abuses in recovering them.” The abuses in today’s Reserve Granaries are indeed of this kind. Selecting suitable people to take charge would eliminate these four abuses. In my humble opinion, it would be appropriate to buy and sell grain without lending it out and collecting repayments.

The responsibility for enriching the people rests above all with the local officials. Chief officials should have their performance assessed primarily by the land brought under cultivation, and assistant officials should make encouraging agriculture their duty. They should be chosen for unadorned sincerity rather than a contrived outward appearance; they should not be prized for their extraction of cocoon silk…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
絲之能而貴其烹鮮之術則有司知勸於
富民矣楚之田與糧不相隸也久矣欲為
一勞永逸之圖則非大更張不可必使田
不失其畔糧不失其額然後革飛詭之弊
釐附蔭之籍懲兼并之豪察攬納之姦禁
告訐之俗約倍息之貸則庶乎民志有定
而富庶自臻矣是當徐議而深謀之耳此
六者楚之所以待而生也夫國依於民民
依於食故惠澤流而下不病民然後貢賦
===
修而上足利國不病民仁之道也利國義
之道也吾以仁始彼以義終上下之分也
感應之理也故荀卿曰田野縣鄙者財之
本也垣窌倉廩者財之末也百姓時和事
業得敘者貨之源也等賦府庫者貨之流
也先後本末之序固如此耳若以為民可
深求而不病而不為之所則失之矣書生
一得之見如此若夫經國之遠猷裕民之
良策則在
punctuated: 絲之能，而貴其烹鮮之術，則有司知勸於富民矣。楚之田與糧不相隸也久矣。欲為一勞永逸之圖，則非大更張不可，必使田不失其畔，糧不失其額，然後革飛詭之弊，釐附蔭之籍，懲兼并之豪，察攬納之姦，禁告訐之俗，約倍息之貸，則庶乎民志有定，而富庶自臻矣。是當徐議而深謀之耳。此六者，楚之所以待而生也。夫國依於民，民依於食，故惠澤流而下，不病民，然後貢賦修而上，足利國。不病民，仁之道也；利國，義之道也。吾以仁始，彼以義終，上下之分也，感應之理也。故荀卿曰：「田野縣鄙者，財之本也；垣窌倉廩者，財之末也；百姓時和，事業得敘者，貨之源也；等賦府庫者，貨之流也。」先後本末之序，固如此耳。若以為民可深求而不病，而不為之所，則失之矣。書生一得之見如此。若夫經國之遠猷、裕民之良策，則在
translation_en:
…skill in extracting silk, but value instead their art of governing as one cooks a small fish, then the responsible officials will know to apply themselves to enriching the people. In Chu, land and grain-tax liabilities have long ceased to correspond. To devise a settlement that will secure lasting ease through a single effort requires a thorough reform. Land must retain its proper boundaries, and grain-tax liabilities their proper quotas. Then abuses involving fraudulent transfers and concealment of tax liabilities must be eliminated; registers of holdings placed under others’ protection must be rectified; powerful men who engross land must be punished; fraud by those who undertake tax payments on others’ behalf must be investigated; the practice of malicious denunciation must be prohibited; and loans charging double interest must be restricted. Only then may the people’s minds become settled and prosperity arise of itself. These matters require deliberate discussion and careful planning. These six measures are what Chu depends upon for its livelihood.

The state depends upon the people, and the people depend upon food. Thus, only when benevolence flows downward without harming the people can tribute and taxes be duly supplied upward, sufficient to benefit the state. Not harming the people is the way of benevolence; benefiting the state is the way of righteousness. We begin with benevolence, and they complete the process with righteousness: these are the respective duties of superiors and inferiors, and the principle of stimulus and response. Thus Xun Qing said: “Fields and outlying settlements are the roots of wealth; enclosed storage pits and granaries are its branches. When the common people enjoy seasonal harmony and their occupations proceed in due order, this is the source of goods; graded taxation and treasuries are their downstream flow.” Such indeed is the proper ordering of what comes first and last, of roots and branches. To suppose that heavy exactions can be imposed upon the people without harming them, and to make no provision for them, would be an error.

Such is this scholar’s modest insight. As for far-reaching plans for ordering the state and sound policies for enriching the people, these lie with …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
廟堂之上愚固不得而與其憂也
第三問
雷孟冬
同考試官敎授沈批周子崛起舂陵倡明斯道
二程因而受之子是之言而其學之傳緒的有可考矣
考試官敎諭黃批言足以達大儒之奧
考試官敎授陳批論學有實見
儒者之於道崛起而能明者性也有所受
而傳者敎也超然獨契於千載之下而聞
===
見知識不與焉則神解也神解者自得之
謂也學不能自得則其求之心也或泥於
意見傳之人也或流於口耳博之事物也
或蕩決於支離破碎况敢望其神解而有
得哉知此始可以論周子之默契矣夫周
子之默契者何道也堯舜以來相傳之正
道也自堯舜至文武周公自文武周公至
孔子自孔子至孟軻而其傳泯焉錯殽于
秦火訓詁于漢儒沉幽于晉魏隋唐雖有
punctuated:
廟堂之上，愚固不得而與其憂也。

第三問
雷孟冬

同考試官敎授沈批：「周子崛起舂陵，倡明斯道，二程因而受之。子是之言，而其學之傳緒的有可考矣。」
考試官敎諭黃批：「言足以達大儒之奧。」
考試官敎授陳批：「論學有實見。」

儒者之於道，崛起而能明者，性也；有所受而傳者，敎也。超然獨契於千載之下，而聞見知識不與焉，則神解也。神解者，自得之謂也。學不能自得，則其求之心也，或泥於意見；傳之人也，或流於口耳；博之事物也，或蕩決於支離破碎。况敢望其神解而有得哉？知此，始可以論周子之默契矣。夫周子之默契者，何道也？堯舜以來相傳之正道也。自堯舜至文武周公，自文武周公至孔子，自孔子至孟軻，而其傳泯焉。錯殽于秦火，訓詁于漢儒，沉幽于晉魏隋唐，雖有
translation_en:
…those in the highest councils of government; I, in my ignorance, am certainly unable to share their concerns.

Third Question
Lei Mengdong

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Prefectural School Instructor: “Master Zhou arose in Chungling and proclaimed and elucidated this Way. The two Cheng brothers then received it from him. Your words affirm this [?], and the lineage through which his learning was transmitted can indeed be traced.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, County School Instructor: “His words suffice to convey the profound insights of the great Confucian masters.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Prefectural School Instructor: “His discussion of learning shows genuine insight.”

For a Confucian scholar, to arise independently and illuminate the Way is a matter of innate nature; to receive it from someone and transmit it is a matter of teaching. To transcend ordinary understanding and attain accord with it unaided a thousand years later, without the participation of knowledge acquired through hearing and seeing, is spiritual apprehension. Spiritual apprehension means attaining understanding for oneself. If one cannot attain understanding for oneself through learning, then the mind that seeks it may become mired in opinions; in transmitting it to others, one may lapse into mere oral repetition; in extending one's learning broadly to affairs and things, one may lose all bounds amid disconnected fragments. How, then, could one dare hope for spiritual apprehension and genuine attainment? Only by understanding this can one begin to discuss Master Zhou's silent accord with the Way.

Now, with what Way did Master Zhou attain silent accord? It was the orthodox Way transmitted from the time of Yao and Shun onward. From Yao and Shun it passed to Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou; from Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou to Confucius; and from Confucius to Meng Ke. Then its transmission disappeared. It became confused amid the Qin book burnings, reduced to textual glosses among the Han scholars, and submerged in obscurity during the Jin, Wei, Sui, and Tang. Although there were…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
一二作者察焉而弗精語焉而弗詳聖人
之學謂之絶焉可也寥寥千百載直至周
子而始續之今觀所著太極圖說易通其
言陰陽五行之秘天地萬物之理死生往
來之變剛柔善惡之實禮樂刑政治天下
之法備矣故其於圖發無極二五之妙於
書闡誠源誠立之旨論聖人中正仁義則
曰主靜立人極懼人於其動失之則曰君
子愼動舉學聖之要則曰無欲則靜虛動
===
直患人以發策决科榮身肥家希世取寵
爲事則曰志伊尹之所志患人以廣聞見
工文詞矜智能慕空寂爲事也則曰學顏
子之所學是皆言之至要而與易書春秋
語孟相出入者也書約而道大文質而義
精秦漢以來誠未有臻斯理者而以上接
孟氏之傳豈不信哉至於陸子靜以無極
太極之說本於老子爲疑蓋易言太極以
理言也老子之言無極以無形言也周子
punctuated:
一二作者察焉而弗精，語焉而弗詳，聖人之學謂之絶焉可也。寥寥千百載，直至周子而始續之。今觀所著《太極圖說》《易通》，其言陰陽五行之秘、天地萬物之理、死生往來之變、剛柔善惡之實、禮樂刑政治天下之法，備矣。故其於圖發無極二五之妙，於書闡誠源誠立之旨。論聖人中正仁義，則曰：「主靜立人極。」懼人於其動失之，則曰：「君子愼動。」舉學聖之要，則曰：「無欲則靜虛動直。」患人以發策决科、榮身肥家、希世取寵爲事，則曰：「志伊尹之所志。」患人以廣聞見、工文詞、矜智能、慕空寂爲事也，則曰：「學顏子之所學。」是皆言之至要，而與《易》《書》《春秋》《語》《孟》相出入者也。書約而道大，文質而義精，秦漢以來誠未有臻斯理者，而以上接孟氏之傳，豈不信哉？

至於陸子靜以無極太極之說本於老子爲疑，蓋《易》言太極，以理言也；老子之言無極，以無形言也。周子
translation_en:
…one or two writers perceived it, but without precision, and spoke of it, but without detail. It would be fair to say that the learning of the sages had died out. For hundreds upon hundreds of years it languished, until Master Zhou first renewed its transmission. Now, examining his Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), we find comprehensive discussions of the mysteries of yin and yang and the Five Phases; the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things; the transformations of death and life, departure and return; the realities of firmness and yielding, goodness and evil; and the methods of governing the world through rites, music, punishments, and administration. Thus, in the diagram he reveals the subtleties of the Nonpolar, the two forces, and the Five Phases; in the book he elucidates the meaning of sincerity as the source and of sincerity’s establishment. Discussing the sage’s centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, he says: “Give primacy to stillness and establish the ultimate standard for humanity.” Fearing that people might go astray in their activity, he says: “The gentleman is cautious in acting.” Summing up the essentials of learning to become a sage, he says: “Without desire, one is empty in stillness and upright in activity.” Concerned that people devote themselves to answering examination questions and winning degrees, bringing glory to themselves and wealth to their families, and courting the age to gain favor, he says: “Aspire to what Yi Yin aspired to.” Concerned that people devote themselves to broadening their knowledge, perfecting their literary compositions, flaunting their intelligence and abilities, and admiring emptiness and quiescence, he says: “Learn what Master Yan learned.” These are all supremely essential statements, consonant with the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Analects, and the Mencius. His writings are concise, yet the Way they convey is great; their language is unadorned, yet their meaning is refined. Truly, since the Qin and Han dynasties, no one had attained these principles. Can we doubt that he reached back to continue the transmission of Master Meng?

As for Lu Zijing’s suspicion that the teaching of the Nonpolar and the Supreme Ultimate originated with Laozi: when the Book of Changes speaks of the Supreme Ultimate, it speaks in terms of principle; when Laozi speaks of the Nonpolar, he speaks in terms of formlessness. Master Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所謂無極而太極正以其實有是理而無
形之可見豈眞若老子無極之云哉晦菴
之所辯者是也朱子發又謂太極圖傳之
穆修修傳先天圖於种放放傳於陳摶夫
摶之長往不返蓋與鳳歌荷篠者伍而非
聖人無可無不可之道況种穆之所著者
又止以古文已乎五峯之所序者是也或
又謂周子與胡文恭同師鶴林壽涯而遂
疑其學之所自出且孔子問禮老聃矣訪
===
樂萇弘矣問官郯子矣謂孔子無所不學
則可而謂孔子之道出於老聃萇弘郯子
可乎是壽涯者亦殆其無常師之一也而
何足以累其默契道體之全哉蓋在當時
人見其政事精絕則以爲宦業過人見其
雅志林壑飄然塵外則以爲有仙風道氣
妻子饔粥不給曠然不以爲意則以爲安
貧無累而未見其大也趙清獻惑於讒而
感悟李初平聽其言而有得荆公聞其語
punctuated: 所謂無極而太極，正以其實有是理而無形之可見，豈眞若老子無極之云哉？晦菴之所辯者是也。朱子發又謂太極圖傳之穆修，修傳先天圖於种放，放傳於陳摶。夫摶之長往不返，蓋與鳳歌荷篠者伍，而非聖人無可無不可之道。況种、穆之所著者，又止以古文已乎？五峯之所序者是也。或又謂周子與胡文恭同師鶴林壽涯，而遂疑其學之所自出。且孔子問禮老聃矣，訪樂萇弘矣，問官郯子矣，謂孔子無所不學則可，而謂孔子之道出於老聃、萇弘、郯子，可乎？是壽涯者，亦殆其無常師之一也，而何足以累其默契道體之全哉？蓋在當時，人見其政事精絕，則以爲宦業過人；見其雅志林壑，飄然塵外，則以爲有仙風道氣；妻子饔粥不給，曠然不以爲意，則以爲安貧無累，而未見其大也。趙清獻惑於讒而感悟，李初平聽其言而有得，荆公聞其語
translation_en:
…what Master Zhou called “Without Ultimate, yet Supreme Ultimate” means precisely that this principle truly exists, though it has no visible form. How could this really be the same as Laozi’s talk of the “Without Ultimate”? This is what Hui’an argued.

Zhu Zifa further maintained that the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate was transmitted by Mu Xiu, that Xiu received the Diagram of the Prior Heaven from Chong Fang, and that Fang received it from Chen Tuan. Now Tuan’s withdrawal from the world, never to return, placed him among such men as the singer of the phoenix song and the bearer of the weeding basket; it was not the sage’s Way of neither insisting upon nor ruling out any course of action. Moreover, did not the writings of Chong and Mu amount merely to ancient-style prose? This is the point made in Wufeng’s preface.

Others have also said that Master Zhou and Hu Wengong both studied under Shouya of Helin, and consequently cast doubt on the source of his learning. Yet Confucius asked Lao Dan about ritual, consulted Chang Hong about music, and questioned the Viscount of Tan about official offices. It is permissible to say that there was nothing Confucius did not study; but can one say that Confucius’s Way originated with Lao Dan, Chang Hong, or the Viscount of Tan? This Shouya was probably simply one of his teachers, since he had no fixed teacher. How could that detract from his silent accord with the whole substance of the Way?

At the time, people saw his consummate skill in government and considered his official achievements superior to those of others. Seeing his refined aspirations toward forests and valleys, as though he floated beyond the dusty world, they thought he possessed the bearing of an immortal and the spirit of a Daoist. When his wife and children lacked sufficient food, he remained serenely unconcerned; people therefore thought he was content in poverty and free of encumbrances. Yet they had not perceived his greatness. Zhao Qingxian, misled by slander, was moved to an awakening; Li Chuping gained understanding by listening to his words; the Duke of Jing heard his remarks …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
精思至忘寢食斯亦大矣而未見其所自
得也黃太史稱其短於取名而樂於求志
薄於徼福而厚於得民菲於奉身而燕及
惇嫠短於希世而尚友千古又謂其胸中
灑落如光風霽月見其所自得矣而未見
其所以教人也至於授之二程而令尋孔
顏樂處則不傳之妙於是而盡洩焉然後
見其學之至也執事乃欲愚也言其所樂
愚將何言乎謂之樂道耶樂物耶求之曲
===
肱飲水耶求之陋巷耶抑求之曲肱飲水
陋巷之外耶蓋周程之去孔子千餘年矣
今去程子又數百年矣周子語之而不發
程子受之說而未言愚也何足以知之雖
然則亦不可以不講也蓋天之生人畀之
以心而道具焉人心之本體無不樂者也
有不樂則物累之也蓋常察見此心之體
有以為吾之主而一切富貴貧賤可喜可
愕之來又儻然以應之而不能為吾動則
punctuated: 精思至忘寢食，斯亦大矣，而未見其所自得也。黃太史稱其短於取名，而樂於求志；薄於徼福，而厚於得民；菲於奉身，而燕及惇嫠；短於希世，而尚友千古。又謂其胸中灑落，如光風霽月。見其所自得矣，而未見其所以教人也。至於授之二程，而令尋孔顏樂處，則不傳之妙於是而盡洩焉，然後見其學之至也。執事乃欲愚也言其所樂，愚將何言乎？謂之樂道耶？樂物耶？求之曲肱飲水耶？求之陋巷耶？抑求之曲肱飲水、陋巷之外耶？蓋周程之去孔子千餘年矣，今去程子又數百年矣。周子語之而不發，程子受之說而未言，愚也何足以知之？雖然，則亦不可以不講也。蓋天之生人，畀之以心，而道具焉。人心之本體，無不樂者也；有不樂，則物累之也。蓋常察見此心之體，有以為吾之主，而一切富貴貧賤、可喜可愕之來，又儻然以應之，而不能為吾動，則
translation_en:
…pondered deeply until he forgot sleep and food. This, too, was great, yet it did not reveal what he had inwardly attained. Grand Scribe Huang praised him as little inclined to seek fame but happy to fulfill his aspirations; sparing in seeking blessings for himself but generous in winning the people’s hearts; frugal in providing for himself, yet extending comfort to the [?] and widows; little inclined to court his age’s favor, but taking the worthies of all antiquity as his friends. He further said that his heart was open and clear, like a fresh breeze and the moon after rain. Here we see what he had inwardly attained, but not yet how he taught others. Only when he instructed the two Cheng brothers and bade them seek wherein Confucius and Yan Hui found joy were the subtleties that had gone untransmitted fully disclosed. Only then do we see the highest attainment of his learning.

You, sir, now wish me, ignorant as I am, to speak of what gave him joy. What can I say? Shall I call it joy in the Way? Joy in things? Shall we seek it in resting one’s head on a bent arm and drinking water? Shall we seek it in a humble alley? Or shall we seek it beyond the bent arm, the drinking of water, and the humble alley? Zhou and the Cheng brothers lived more than a thousand years after Confucius; several hundred more years now separate us from Master Cheng. Master Zhou spoke of it without elucidating it; Master Cheng received his teaching without putting it into words. How could someone as ignorant as I be capable of knowing it?

Nevertheless, we cannot leave it undiscussed. When Heaven brings human beings into existence, it endows them with a heart, within which the Way is fully present. In its original substance, the human heart is never without joy. If joy is absent, it is because things encumber it. If we constantly discern the substance of this heart, thereby having something to serve as our master, and respond with equanimity to whatever comes—wealth and honor, poverty and lowliness, occasions for delight or alarm—so that these cannot move us, then…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
我之一心豈不湛然澄徹至虛配天至廣
配地至有配萬物而超然宇宙之外哉孔
子之樂在其中樂乎此也顏子之不改其
樂不改乎此也周子之令尋樂尋乎此也
程子得之吟風弄月以歸吟弄乎此也是
其傳受之真亦已盡矣又安求所謂天理
者而體貼之乎此愚所謂有所受而神解
之說也何也可以言傳者道之槩也言之
所不能盡者則修爲之次第也旣竭吾才
===
而後博約之敎明三省吾身而後一貫之
旨達此聖學也孟子曰可欲之謂善有諸
已之謂信天理者可欲之善也體貼出來
者有諸已之謂信也自其真機而言謂之
樂自其天然條理而言謂之天理樂與天
理也非二物也尋樂之與體貼也亦非二
功也特其生熟淺深殊焉耳自今觀之動
定靜定之書其與主靜之說何如學者須
先識仁其與無欲爲要者何如接人一團
punctuated: 我之一心豈不湛然澄徹，至虛配天，至廣配地，至有配萬物，而超然宇宙之外哉？孔子之樂在其中，樂乎此也；顏子之不改其樂，不改乎此也；周子之令尋樂，尋乎此也；程子得之，吟風弄月以歸，吟弄乎此也。是其傳受之真，亦已盡矣，又安求所謂天理者而體貼之乎？此愚所謂有所受而神解之說也。何也？可以言傳者，道之槩也；言之所不能盡者，則修爲之次第也。旣竭吾才，而後博約之敎明；三省吾身，而後一貫之旨達。此聖學也。孟子曰：「可欲之謂善，有諸已之謂信。」天理者，可欲之善也；體貼出來者，有諸已之謂信也。自其真機而言，謂之樂；自其天然條理而言，謂之天理。樂與天理也，非二物也；尋樂之與體貼也，亦非二功也，特其生熟淺深殊焉耳。自今觀之，「動定靜定」之書，其與「主靜」之說何如？「學者須先識仁」，其與「無欲爲要」者何如？「接人一團
translation_en: …would not my own heart then be limpid and clear, matching Heaven in its utter emptiness, Earth in its utmost breadth, and the myriad things in its fullness of being, while transcending the universe? When Confucius said that joy lay within, this was what he rejoiced in. When Master Yan did not relinquish his joy, this was what he retained. When Master Zhou instructed others to seek joy, this was what they were to seek. When Master Cheng attained it and returned home chanting in the breeze and delighting in the moon, this was what inspired his chanting and delight. The true substance of what they transmitted and received is fully expressed here. Why, then, seek something called heavenly principle and strive to apprehend it inwardly? This is what I mean by receiving a teaching and understanding it intuitively. Why is this so? What words can transmit is the broad outline of the Way; what words cannot fully convey is the sequence of personal cultivation. Only after exhausting all my abilities does the teaching of broadening learning and restraining oneself become clear; only after examining myself on three counts does the meaning of the single thread running through all become comprehensible. This is the learning of the sages. Mencius said: “What is desirable is called goodness; possessing it in oneself is called genuineness.” Heavenly principle is this desirable goodness; inwardly apprehending and realizing it is what is meant by possessing it in oneself and thus being genuine. In terms of its authentic animating impulse, it is called joy; in terms of its natural order, it is called heavenly principle. Joy and heavenly principle are not two separate things; seeking joy and inwardly apprehending principle are likewise not two separate kinds of effort. They differ only in degrees of unfamiliarity or mastery, shallowness or depth. Viewed now, how does the written statement “Be settled in movement and settled in stillness” compare with the teaching of “taking stillness as the governing principle”? How does “Students must first recognize benevolence” compare with “Freedom from desire is essential”? “In dealing with others, a whole spirit of…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
和氣其與襟懷灑落者何如記曰善歌者
使人繼其聲善教者使人繼其志程子之
體貼也不為繼志已乎執事謂明道得之
周子而以伊川謂得不傳之學於遺經為
疑嗟乎此誠愚之所未喻也夫人之氣質
有偶而契者有偶而不相契者而其知與
不知亦繫焉伯淳之於周子類也正叔稍
嚴毅矣然而受學於處同每令尋仲尼顔
子樂處同其所以受易説易通者同故見
===
而知之者得之人也聞而知之者求之經
也今固受之周子矣而謂盡得之遺經可
乎此誠愚之所未喻也豈以周子之學至
伯淳而益光而遂以為言乎夫周子之倡
道也如日之初曙然得二程而授之則日
升矣又得伊洛諸賢相聚而講明之則日
之中天矣夫見日之中天也以為異於初
曙者而遂以為言乎未可知也子靜嘗謂
二程雖同見茂叔後來正叔意思已失愚
punctuated:
和氣，其與襟懷灑落者何如？《記》曰：「善歌者，使人繼其聲；善教者，使人繼其志。」程子之體貼也，不為繼志已乎？執事謂明道得之周子，而以伊川謂得不傳之學於遺經為疑。嗟乎！此誠愚之所未喻也。夫人之氣質，有偶而契者，有偶而不相契者，而其知與不知亦繫焉。伯淳之於周子，類也；正叔稍嚴毅矣。然而受學於處同，每令尋仲尼顔子樂處同，其所以受易説易通者同。故見而知之者，得之人也；聞而知之者，求之經也。今固受之周子矣，而謂盡得之遺經，可乎？此誠愚之所未喻也。
豈以周子之學至伯淳而益光，而遂以為言乎？夫周子之倡道也，如日之初曙然；得二程而授之，則日升矣；又得伊洛諸賢相聚而講明之，則日之中天矣。夫見日之中天也，以為異於初曙者，而遂以為言乎？未可知也。子靜嘗謂：「二程雖同見茂叔，後來正叔意思已失。」愚
translation_en:
…a genial manner: how does this compare with an open and unencumbered disposition? The Record of Rites says: “A good singer makes others carry on his voice; a good teacher makes others carry on his purpose.” Was Master Cheng’s personally apprehending principle not precisely a continuation of that purpose? You say that Mingdao acquired his learning from Master Zhou, yet raise a doubt on the grounds that Yichuan claimed to have acquired learning whose transmission had been broken from the surviving classics. Alas! This is truly something I do not understand. People’s temperaments sometimes happen to accord and sometimes do not, and their understanding or lack of understanding also depends upon this. Bochun was akin to Master Zhou in temperament; Zhengshu was somewhat sterner and more resolute. Yet they studied in the same place [?], were alike repeatedly instructed to seek the source of Zhongni’s and Yanzi’s joy, and were alike in receiving teachings on the Changes and explanations of the Changes and the Comprehensive Writings [?]. Thus, those who understand through seeing acquire their understanding from a person; those who understand through hearing seek it in the classics. Since he certainly received instruction from Master Zhou, can one say that he acquired everything from the surviving classics? This is truly something I do not understand.
Could it be that you make this claim because Master Zhou’s learning became still more illustrious through Bochun? When Master Zhou first proclaimed the Way, it was like the sun at dawn. When he found the two Cheng brothers and instructed them, the sun rose. When the various worthies of the Yi and Luo region subsequently gathered to discuss and elucidate it, the sun reached the middle of the heavens. Seeing the sun at its zenith, do you regard it as different from the sun at dawn and therefore make this claim? I cannot tell. Zijing once said: “Although the two Cheng brothers both met Maoshu, Zhengshu later lost the original sense of his teaching.” I …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
亦未敢以爲然也愚之距周子若此其未
遠也地之相近若此其甚也然於周子之
學則茫如也今以執事之間因之以求二
程因二程以求周子因周子以求孔顏蓋
實有志焉而未能也唯進而敎之
第四問
童承契
考試官敎諭黃批是篇因時勢考人材最精
卒歸之鄭大夫漢武侯之正可以觀史筆矣
===
考試官敎授陳批筆陣嚴整品藻確焉
事無定形揆諸理以論事則失得明矣人
無定品原諸心以論人則賢否辨矣故事
不可以一端裁其事同其所處不同吾從
而求諸理者所以定揆事之衡也不然則
泥人不可以一律觀其人同其所遇不同
吾從而求諸心者所以定知人之鑑也不
然則淆執事舉春秋三國之事機人品之
相類者而詢其說於諸生由百世之後等
punctuated:
亦未敢以爲然也。愚之距周子，若此其未遠也；地之相近，若此其甚也。然於周子之學，則茫如也。今以執事之間，因之以求二程，因二程以求周子，因周子以求孔顏，蓋實有志焉而未能也。唯進而敎之。
第四問
童承契
考試官敎諭黃批：是篇因時勢考人材最精，卒歸之鄭大夫、漢武侯之正，可以觀史筆矣。
考試官敎授陳批：筆陣嚴整，品藻確焉。
事無定形，揆諸理以論事，則失得明矣；人無定品，原諸心以論人，則賢否辨矣。故事不可以一端裁，其事同，其所處不同，吾從而求諸理者，所以定揆事之衡也，不然則泥。人不可以一律觀，其人同，其所遇不同，吾從而求諸心者，所以定知人之鑑也，不然則淆。執事舉春秋、三國之事機、人品之相類者，而詢其說於諸生，由百世之後等
translation_en:
…I likewise dare not regard this as correct. My distance in time from Master Zhou is so slight, and our geographical proximity so great; yet I remain utterly at sea concerning his learning. Now, through the opportunity afforded by you [?], I would seek understanding of the two Cheng masters; through them, of Master Zhou; and through Master Zhou, of Confucius and Yan Hui. I do indeed aspire to this, but have not yet attained it. I ask only that you admit me to your instruction.
Fourth Question
Tong Chengqi
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: This essay is exceptionally discerning in assessing men’s abilities in light of the circumstances of their times. Ultimately, it takes as its standard the rectitude of the Grand Master of Zheng and the Martial Marquis of Han. Here one can discern the historian’s craft.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: The writing is marshalled with rigor and order, and its appraisals are sound.
Affairs have no fixed form. If we assess them by principle, their successes and failures become clear. People have no fixed classification. If we assess them by tracing their intentions to their source, their worthiness or unworthiness becomes distinguishable. Thus affairs cannot be judged from a single standpoint: the affairs may be alike, but their circumstances differ. Seeking the principles underlying them establishes a balance by which to weigh affairs; otherwise, one becomes rigid. People cannot be viewed according to a single rule: the people may be alike, but what they encounter differs. Seeking the intentions in their hearts establishes a mirror by which to understand people; otherwise, distinctions become confused. You have selected comparable situations and human characters from the Spring and Autumn and Three Kingdoms periods and asked us students to explain them. From a hundred generations later, to assess…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
百世之前如之何其莫之違也聊即所聞
而復之粤自皇帝王霸世道升降風氣會
流其來遠矣周轍既東王綱漸解侯國盛
而霸圖興大雅亡而春秋作蓋不幸而不
知有王猶幸而尚知有霸蓋霸也者所以
倡諸國而使知有王者也有霸則庶幾乎
有王矣于時齊桓合諸侯攘夷狄以尊周
室控大扶小而王室之難定束牲載書而
天子之禁明可謂盛矣晉文繼霸修齊桓
===
之業城濮一戰克楚師而遂以威服踐土
一盟奬王室而能以德攻蓋亦幾焉但其
意則欲天下之宗巳而非有尊王之實故
謂之挾天子以令諸侯周室之所以終於
不競也下此又不足言矣東漢之末也董
卓竊李郭逆獻帝播越而天下無君有能
興桓文之事則亦可以有辭於天下矣孫
權據有江東袁紹稱雄冀北劉備以帝室
之胄而不能伸信義於天下曹操起而收
punctuated:
百世之前，如之何其莫之違也？聊即所聞而復之。粤自皇帝王霸，世道升降，風氣會流，其來遠矣。周轍既東，王綱漸解，侯國盛而霸圖興，大雅亡而春秋作。蓋不幸而不知有王，猶幸而尚知有霸。蓋霸也者，所以倡諸國而使知有王者也。有霸則庶幾乎有王矣。于時齊桓合諸侯，攘夷狄，以尊周室；控大扶小，而王室之難定；束牲載書，而天子之禁明，可謂盛矣。晉文繼霸，修齊桓之業，城濮一戰，克楚師而遂以威服；踐土一盟，奬王室而能以德攻，蓋亦幾焉。但其意則欲天下之宗巳，而非有尊王之實，故謂之挾天子以令諸侯。周室之所以終於不競也。下此又不足言矣。
東漢之末也，董卓竊，李郭逆，獻帝播越，而天下無君。有能興桓文之事，則亦可以有辭於天下矣。孫權據有江東，袁紹稱雄冀北，劉備以帝室之胄，而不能伸信義於天下，曹操起而收
translation_en:
… a hundred generations earlier—how can our judgments accord with those events without discrepancy? Let me offer a reply based on what I have learned. From the ages of the august sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons, the world's order has risen and fallen, and prevailing influences have converged and spread: this history reaches far back. Once the Zhou royal carriage moved east, royal authority gradually unraveled. The feudal states grew powerful and ambitions for hegemony arose; the spirit of the Greater Odes disappeared, and the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed. It was unfortunate that men no longer acknowledged a king, but fortunate that they still acknowledged a hegemon. A hegemon was one who led the various states and made them acknowledge the king. With a hegemon, there was at least some prospect of having a king acknowledged.
At that time, Duke Huan of Qi assembled the feudal lords and repelled the Yi and Di peoples to uphold the house of Zhou. He restrained the great states and supported the small, settling the royal house's troubles; with bound sacrificial animals and written covenants, he made the Son of Heaven's prohibitions clear. His achievements may indeed be called splendid. Duke Wen of Jin succeeded to the hegemony and carried forward Duke Huan of Qi's work. In the battle at Chengpu, he defeated the Chu army and thereby secured submission through his might; at the covenant of Jiantu, he supported the royal house and was able to attack through virtue [?]. He too came close to the ideal. Yet his intention was to have all under Heaven acknowledge him as their leader, without truly honoring the king. Hence this was called ‘holding the Son of Heaven in one's power to command the feudal lords.’ This explains why the house of Zhou ultimately remained powerless. Those who came afterward are still less worth discussing.
At the end of the Eastern Han, Dong Zhuo usurped power, Li Jue and Guo Si rebelled, Emperor Xian was driven into exile, and all under Heaven were left without a ruler. Had anyone been able to revive the undertakings of Dukes Huan and Wen, he could have offered a defensible account of himself to the world. Sun Quan occupied Jiangdong; Yuan Shao asserted his supremacy in Jibei; Liu Bei, though a descendant of the imperial house, could not extend good faith and righteousness throughout the realm. Cao Cao rose and gathered …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
衆人之遺策刼帝遷許奉辭伐罪蓋自謂
霸世之遺業忠國之令圖也而不知由君
子視之直漢賊耳蓋以天子爲奇貨而居
之矣曾是以爲尊王也乎至此則非惟不
知有王亦不知有霸矣不亦重可慨耶若
中間事機之失得人品之賢否則亦有可
言者春秋之楚三國之吳皆江漢之國也
齊桓合諸侯以伐楚楚人遂帖召陵之盟
曹操下荆州而伐吳吳人反成赤壁之勝
===
非楚無方城漢水而吳獨有長江也齊桓
包茅之責授楚以必承之罪屈完所謂以
德綏諸侯誰敢不服者也若曹操之廢漢
自立則無名矣用舟師而失其利信僞降
而中其術操焉得而不敗也君子謂吳之
是舉也不爲幸楚之於江黃蜀之於吳皆
與國也齊盟江黃爲伐楚也楚滅黃而齊
不能救蜀好江東爲伐魏也魏破蜀而吳
不能援非齊之遠黃而吳之遠蜀也齊桓
punctuated: 衆人之遺策，刼帝遷許，奉辭伐罪，蓋自謂霸世之遺業、忠國之令圖也。而不知由君子視之，直漢賊耳！蓋以天子爲奇貨而居之矣，曾是以爲尊王也乎？至此則非惟不知有王，亦不知有霸矣，不亦重可慨耶？若中間事機之失得、人品之賢否，則亦有可言者。春秋之楚、三國之吳，皆江漢之國也。齊桓合諸侯以伐楚，楚人遂帖召陵之盟；曹操下荆州而伐吳，吳人反成赤壁之勝。非楚無方城、漢水，而吳獨有長江也。齊桓包茅之責，授楚以必承之罪，屈完所謂「以德綏諸侯，誰敢不服」者也。若曹操之廢漢自立，則無名矣。用舟師而失其利，信僞降而中其術，操焉得而不敗也？君子謂吳之是舉也，不爲幸。楚之於江黃、蜀之於吳，皆與國也。齊盟江黃，爲伐楚也；楚滅黃，而齊不能救。蜀好江東，爲伐魏也；魏破蜀，而吳不能援。非齊之遠黃，而吳之遠蜀也。齊桓
translation_en:
…the stratagems others had left unused, seized the emperor and moved him to Xu, and invoked imperial commands to punish the guilty. He presumably regarded this as carrying on the legacy of the age of hegemons and as an excellent plan for serving the state loyally. Yet he did not realize that, in the eyes of the noble man, he was simply a traitor to the Han! He treated the Son of Heaven as a rare commodity to be acquired and held. Could this possibly count as honoring the king? At this point he understood neither kingship nor even hegemony. Is this not all the more lamentable?
As for successes and failures in handling the circumstances, and the worthiness or unworthiness of the men involved, there is also something to be said. Chu in the Spring and Autumn period and Wu in the Three Kingdoms period were both states of the Yangzi and Han river region. Duke Huan of Qi assembled the regional lords to attack Chu, and the people of Chu duly submitted to the covenant at Shaoling. Cao Cao took Jingzhou and attacked Wu, yet the people of Wu instead achieved victory at Chibi. It was not that Chu lacked Fangcheng and the Han River, while Wu alone possessed the Yangzi River. Duke Huan’s demand concerning the tribute of bundled thatching grass charged Chu with an offense it was bound to acknowledge. This was what Qu Wan meant when he said, “If you bring peace to the regional lords through virtue, who would dare not submit?” Cao Cao’s attempt to overthrow the Han and establish himself, however, lacked a legitimate justification. He employed naval forces but forfeited their advantages; he trusted a feigned surrender and fell into the enemy’s trap. How could Cao Cao have avoided defeat? The noble man holds that Wu’s achievement on this occasion was no mere stroke of luck.
Chu’s relationship with Jiang and Huang, and Shu’s relationship with Wu, were in each case relationships between allied states [?]. Qi allied with Jiang and Huang in order to attack Chu; yet when Chu destroyed Huang, Qi could not rescue it. Shu cultivated friendly relations with Jiangdong in order to attack Wei; yet when Wei defeated Shu, Wu could not come to its aid. It was not because Qi was distant from Huang or Wu distant from Shu. Duke Huan of Qi…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
怠荒已形俇潢無可恃之力管仲所謂伐
而不能救無以宗諸侯者也若孫吳之僅
知自存則失計矣徘徊老壽春之師廢立
成內亂之政蜀焉得而有賴也君子謂吳
之相繼也不為過秦穆之用孟明也收三
敗之績以霸西戎楚成之誅得臣也成再
敗之實以資敵國夫馬謖街亭之一敗孔
明宜鑒于茲矣而必誅之蓋孔明方弘討
賊之義若不誅則無以勵士而定眾也況
===
街亭之役係國存亡謖其可免耶救鄭之
舉欒書違眾帥之欲釋蔡而還師會吳之
役荀罃違二帥之請圍偪陽而致克夫司
馬懿渭南之請戰曹叡宜假其權矣而必
以辛毗止之蓋懿本無欲戰之情若不請
則無以示武而飾慙也且閫外之寄將軍
制之懿其有不知耶事幾之失得其槩如
此較其大者而論之桓公之伐楚不能正
其僭王之罪吳蜀之破操不能訖其篡漢
punctuated: 怠荒已形，俇潢無可恃之力，管仲所謂「伐而不能救，無以宗諸侯」者也。若孫吳之僅知自存，則失計矣。徘徊老壽春之師，廢立成內亂之政，蜀焉得而有賴也？君子謂吳之相繼也，不為過。秦穆之用孟明也，收三敗之績以霸西戎；楚成之誅得臣也，成再敗之實以資敵國。夫馬謖街亭之一敗，孔明宜鑒于茲矣，而必誅之，蓋孔明方弘討賊之義，若不誅，則無以勵士而定眾也。況街亭之役係國存亡，謖其可免耶？救鄭之舉，欒書違眾帥之欲，釋蔡而還師；會吳之役，荀罃違二帥之請，圍偪陽而致克。夫司馬懿渭南之請戰，曹叡宜假其權矣，而必以辛毗止之，蓋懿本無欲戰之情，若不請，則無以示武而飾慙也。且閫外之寄，將軍制之，懿其有不知耶？事幾之失得，其槩如此。較其大者而論之，桓公之伐楚，不能正其僭王之罪；吳蜀之破操，不能訖其篡漢
translation_en:
…his indolence and neglect had already become apparent; in his agitation [?], he had no strength on which to rely. This was what Guan Zhong meant by saying, “To attack but be unable to rescue leaves one no means of leading the regional lords.” As for the Sun house’s state of Wu, knowing only how to preserve itself was a failure of strategy. Its army lingered at Shouchun until it was worn out, while the deposition and installation of rulers brought internal disorder to its government. How could Shu have relied upon it? The gentleman considers it no exaggeration to say that Wu followed in its wake [in falling?].

Duke Mu of Qin employed Mengming and, recovering from three defeats, achieved hegemony over the Western Rong. King Cheng of Chu executed Dechen, thereby effectively suffering a second defeat and strengthening an enemy state. Surely Kongming ought to have taken warning from this when Ma Su suffered his single defeat at Jieting; yet he insisted on executing him. This was because Kongming was then advancing the righteous cause of punishing the rebels: without executing Ma Su, he would have had no means of spurring on his soldiers and steadying the army. Moreover, the engagement at Jieting bore upon the state's very survival. Could Su have been spared?

When marching to rescue Zheng, Luan Shu went against the wishes of the other commanders, left Cai alone, and brought his army back. During the expedition to meet with Wu, Xun Ying went against the request of two commanders, besieged Biyang, and took it. When Sima Yi requested permission to fight south of the Wei River, Cao Rui seemingly ought to have granted him authority; yet he insisted on sending Xin Pi to restrain him. This was because Yi had no actual desire to fight: without requesting battle, however, he would have had no means of displaying martial resolve and concealing his shame. Besides, command beyond the capital's gates is entrusted to the general, who exercises discretion over it. Could Yi have been unaware of this?

Such, in broad outline, are the successes and failures in responding to the critical circumstances of affairs. If we assess and discuss the greater issues, Duke Huan's attack on Chu failed to bring it to account for the crime of usurping the royal title; Wu and Shu's defeat of Cao Cao failed to carry through the punishment for his usurpation of the Han…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之誅孔明以言取人亦昧知人之鑑仲達
握兵自植遂蓄無君之心君子之所以致
惜也生我父母知我鮑叔管仲有是言也
而所事則不同及仲成射鈎之仇鮑設檻
車之術而仲始爲小白用也孔明伏龍士
元鳳雛龐德公有是評也而所就則不同
及魯肅遺書之薦孔明乗間之言而後統
始爲先主用也是非鮑葛違相致之義管
龐昧擇君之明出處之初各因其所遇耳
===
然於此而終知管仲之仁龐統之智矣夾
谷之會晏子寔從乎景公而不能止其登
壇之譟及感於孔子之禮義而始謝之以
質也赤壁之戰孔明寔助乎周瑜而忽動
其相圖之心及藉乎魯肅之調護而始借
之以地也是非嬰有顯君之忠瑜有决事
之智淺夫之中自不能容物耳然於此而
益知孔子之聖孔明之賢矣荀彧度袁紹
之諸臣以破孔融之說使操也一戰而成
punctuated:
之誅。孔明以言取人，亦昧知人之鑑；仲達握兵自植，遂蓄無君之心，君子之所以致惜也。「生我父母，知我鮑叔」，管仲有是言也，而所事則不同。及仲成射鈎之仇，鮑設檻車之術，而仲始爲小白用也。「孔明伏龍，士元鳳雛」，龐德公有是評也，而所就則不同。及魯肅遺書之薦，孔明乗間之言，而後統始爲先主用也。是非鮑葛違相致之義，管龐昧擇君之明，出處之初，各因其所遇耳。
然於此而終知管仲之仁、龐統之智矣。夾谷之會，晏子寔從乎景公，而不能止其登壇之譟，及感於孔子之禮義，而始謝之以質也。赤壁之戰，孔明寔助乎周瑜，而忽動其相圖之心，及藉乎魯肅之調護，而始借之以地也。是非嬰有顯君之忠，瑜有决事之智，淺夫之中，自不能容物耳。然於此而益知孔子之聖、孔明之賢矣。荀彧度袁紹之諸臣，以破孔融之說，使操也一戰而成
translation_en:
…the punishment due for his usurpation of Han. Kongming judged men by their words, likewise showing a failure of discernment in assessing character; Zhongda held military power to establish his own position and thus harbored a heart that acknowledged no sovereign. These are matters that the gentleman deplores. “My parents gave me life; Uncle Bao understands me”: Guan Zhong said this, yet the two served different masters. Only after Guan Zhong had incurred enmity by shooting Xiaobai’s belt hook, and Bao had devised the stratagem of the prison cart, did Guan Zhong enter Xiaobai’s service. “Kongming is the Crouching Dragon; Shiyuan is the Phoenix Fledgling”: Pang Degong made this appraisal, yet the two attached themselves to different masters. Only after Lu Su recommended Pang Tong by letter and Kongming spoke on his behalf at an opportune moment did Tong enter the service of the Former Lord, Liu Bei. This was not because Bao and Zhuge failed in their obligation to recommend others, or because Guan Zhong and Pang Tong lacked discernment in choosing a lord. At the outset of their decisions to serve or withdraw, each simply followed the circumstances he encountered.
Yet from this we ultimately recognize Guan Zhong’s benevolence and Pang Tong’s wisdom. At the meeting at Jiagu, Master Yan indeed accompanied Duke Jing, yet could not stop the clamorous intrusion onto the platform. Only when moved by Confucius’s ritual propriety and righteousness did he offer an apology backed by a pledge [?]. At the battle of Chibi, Kongming indeed assisted Zhou Yu, yet Zhou Yu suddenly began to entertain designs against him. Only through Lu Su’s mediation and protection did he finally lend him territory. This was not an instance of Yan Ying’s loyalty in bringing distinction to his lord, or of Zhou Yu’s wisdom in deciding affairs: narrow-minded men simply cannot accommodate others. Yet from this we recognize all the more clearly Confucius’s sageliness and Kongming’s worthiness. Xun Yu assessed Yuan Shao’s various advisers to refute Kong Rong’s argument, enabling Cao Cao to achieve success in a single battle…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
可謂長於料人矣而楚之嬖人伍參者先
能之楚是以有邲之捷賈詡度曹操之還
師以敎張繡之追使繡也再戰而克可謂
長於料事矣而魯之賤士曹劌者先能之
魯是以有長勺之捷大抵春秋之世先王
之敎化未泯人猶襲流風以成其智不可
以其嬖與賤者而少之也子貢之長於言
語也一說吳而足以存魯趙咨爲吳使魏
乃亦以其誇詡之詞而致上國之信焉子
===
產之善於辭命也屢使晉而足以寬鄭鄧
芝爲蜀使吳乃復以其口舌之力而結同
仇之盟焉大抵秦漢而下戰國之從橫未
息人猶沿習氣以見其能未可以其誇與
狂者而多之也人品之高下其槩如此較
其大者而論之晏嬰之不知孔子固周道
之不興周瑜之不容孔明亦漢祚之不復
荀彧之助操無取於死漢而徇名賈詡之
助繡無取於降操而徇利君子之所以致
punctuated: 可謂長於料人矣，而楚之嬖人伍參者先能之，楚是以有邲之捷。賈詡度曹操之還師，以敎張繡之追，使繡也再戰而克，可謂長於料事矣，而魯之賤士曹劌者先能之，魯是以有長勺之捷。大抵春秋之世，先王之敎化未泯，人猶襲流風以成其智，不可以其嬖與賤者而少之也。子貢之長於言語也，一說吳而足以存魯；趙咨爲吳使魏，乃亦以其誇詡之詞而致上國之信焉。子產之善於辭命也，屢使晉而足以寬鄭；鄧芝爲蜀使吳，乃復以其口舌之力而結同仇之盟焉。大抵秦漢而下，戰國之從橫未息，人猶沿習氣以見其能，未可以其誇與狂者而多之也。人品之高下，其槩如此。較其大者而論之，晏嬰之不知孔子，固周道之不興；周瑜之不容孔明，亦漢祚之不復。荀彧之助操，無取於死漢而徇名；賈詡之助繡，無取於降操而徇利。君子之所以致
translation_en:
…he may be called adept at judging men. Yet Wu Can, a favored courtier of Chu, had already shown this ability, and through it Chu gained victory at Bi. Jia Xu assessed Cao Cao’s withdrawal and instructed Zhang Xiu in pursuing him, enabling Xiu to win when he fought a second time. He may be called adept at judging circumstances. Yet Cao Gui, a man of low standing in Lu, had already shown this ability, and through it Lu gained victory at Changshao. Broadly speaking, in the Spring and Autumn period, the moral instruction of the former kings had not yet faded away. People still inherited its lingering influence and thereby developed their wisdom. They should not be held in low esteem merely because they were favorites or men of humble standing.

Zigong excelled in speech: a single persuasive appeal to Wu sufficed to preserve Lu. Zhao Zi, serving as Wu’s envoy to Wei, likewise secured the trust of that superior state through his boastful words. Zichan excelled in diplomatic language: his repeated missions to Jin sufficed to ease the pressure on Zheng. Deng Zhi, serving as Shu’s envoy to Wu, likewise used the power of his tongue to forge an alliance against a common enemy. Broadly speaking, from the Qin and Han onward, the practices of the Warring States’ vertical and horizontal alliances had not ceased. People still followed these ingrained habits to display their abilities. They should not therefore be highly esteemed for their boasting and bravado.

Such, in outline, are the distinctions between higher and lower character. Comparing and discussing the weightier matters, Yan Ying’s failure to recognize Confucius certainly contributed to the failure of the Way of Zhou to flourish; Zhou Yu’s inability to tolerate Kongming likewise contributed to the failure to restore the Han imperial succession. Xun Yu assisted Cao Cao: there is nothing to commend in his dying for the Han while pursuing reputation. Jia Xu assisted Zhang Xiu: there is nothing to commend in his surrendering to Cao Cao while pursuing advantage. These are the reasons why the gentleman feels …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
惜也雖然君子遇天下之事未必無與古
人同者顧吾所以當之何如耳吾以理而
論古人之事不可以吾事而違於理吾以
心而論古人之品不可以吾躬而失其心
夫子萬世準繩固所當學矣論其次於春
秋得一人焉曰子產於三國得一人焉曰
孔明子產讓不失禮而車服之必辭忠以
損怨而鄉校之不毁爭承去公侯之貢爲
國基也養民致輿人之誦爲遺愛也春秋
===
===
之賢有能如之者乎孔明隆中三顧得出
處之中行出師二表明漢賊之大義開誠
布公王佐之才也寧靜致遠禮樂之具也
三國之賢有能如之者乎鄭國間於晉楚
而勢終於不振蜀漢弱於吳魏而業隳於
垂成固非二子之罪也愚生不敏敢取師
焉爲其正而已矣尚友之說惟執事教之
第五問
banxin: 鄉試錄 八十六 程沂
punctuated:
惜也。雖然，君子遇天下之事，未必無與古人同者，顧吾所以當之何如耳。吾以理而論古人之事，不可以吾事而違於理；吾以心而論古人之品，不可以吾躬而失其心。夫子萬世準繩，固所當學矣。論其次，於春秋得一人焉，曰子產；於三國得一人焉，曰孔明。子產讓不失禮，而車服之必辭；忠以損怨，而鄉校之不毁。爭承去公侯之貢，爲國基也；養民致輿人之誦，爲遺愛也。春秋之賢，有能如之者乎？孔明隆中三顧，得出處之中行；出師二表，明漢賊之大義。開誠布公，王佐之才也；寧靜致遠，禮樂之具也。三國之賢，有能如之者乎？鄭國間於晉楚，而勢終於不振；蜀漢弱於吳魏，而業隳於垂成。固非二子之罪也。愚生不敏，敢取師焉，爲其正而已矣。尚友之說，惟執事教之。

第五問
translation_en:
…is what the gentleman finds regrettable. Nevertheless, when a gentleman encounters affairs in the world, some may well resemble those encountered by the ancients; the question is simply how we respond to them. If I judge the deeds of the ancients by principle, I must not violate principle in my own affairs. If I judge their character by the moral heart, I must not myself lose that heart. The Master, Confucius, is the standard for ten thousand generations and certainly the one we ought to emulate. Among those next to him, I find one man in the Spring and Autumn period, Zichan, and one in the Three Kingdoms period, Kongming.

Zichan’s modest yielding did not depart from ritual propriety, and he firmly declined gifts of carriages and robes. Through loyal service he diminished resentment, and he did not demolish the village schools. By contesting and removing the tribute demanded by dukes and marquises [?], he laid a foundation for the state; by nurturing the people until ordinary men sang his praises, he left a legacy of affection. Among the worthy men of the Spring and Autumn period, was there anyone who could equal him?

In responding to the three visits at Longzhong, Kongming attained the proper mean between entering office and remaining in retirement. In his two Memorials on Sending Out the Army, he clarified the great moral distinction between the Han and the rebels. His candor and impartiality showed the talent of one fit to assist a true king; his tranquility and pursuit of far-reaching aims showed his capacity for ritual and music. Among the worthy men of the Three Kingdoms period, was there anyone who could equal him?

Zheng lay between Jin and Chu, and its power ultimately failed to revive; Shu Han was weaker than Wu and Wei, and its undertaking collapsed when success was near. These were certainly not the faults of those two men. Dull-witted student that I am, I venture to take them as my teachers solely because of their rectitude. On the principle of befriending the ancients, I respectfully ask you for instruction.

Fifth Question

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭潘批苗夷不可語訓久矣我
國家張置控壓深合古虞分北之理乃者約束稍弛遂成搶攘必復處
置得宜而服其心此則不可易之策
同考試官教授林批夷落孰非臣子
天威在上孰敢越志第法敝人玩再須一整頓耳是篇區畫精詳具見經
濟之略
考試官教諭黃批據實論事斐然成章
考試官教授陳批言皆可見之行
治夷之道三恩威信而已恩也者遂其竝
===
生者也威也者堅其不叛者也信也者所
以行乎其恩與威者也綏之以恩震之以
威而弗孚之以信則褻於恩而黷於威褻
於恩而不足以綏也則生戎心黷於威而
不足以震也則墮軍實如是而以為善治
夷者否也夫夷之在西南其種類繁矣若
介川湖貴竹而居者古謂之武陵蠻或曰
三苗之後或曰槃瓠之遺莫有知其所由
來也居則環箐以為圉刀耕火種以為食
punctuated:
同考試官教諭潘批：苗夷不可語訓久矣！我國家張置控壓，深合古虞分北之理。乃者約束稍弛，遂成搶攘，必復處置得宜而服其心，此則不可易之策。
同考試官教授林批：夷落孰非臣子？天威在上，孰敢越志？第法敝人玩，再須一整頓耳。是篇區畫精詳，具見經濟之略。
考試官教諭黃批：據實論事，斐然成章。
考試官教授陳批：言皆可見之行。
治夷之道三：恩、威、信而已。恩也者，遂其竝生者也；威也者，堅其不叛者也；信也者，所以行乎其恩與威者也。綏之以恩，震之以威，而弗孚之以信，則褻於恩而黷於威。褻於恩而不足以綏也，則生戎心；黷於威而不足以震也，則墮軍實。如是而以為善治夷者，否也。夫夷之在西南，其種類繁矣。若介川湖貴竹而居者，古謂之武陵蠻，或曰三苗之後，或曰槃瓠之遺，莫有知其所由來也。居則環箐以為圉，刀耕火種以為食，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor in a county Confucian school: It has long been impossible to reason with and instruct the Miao tribes! Our dynasty’s arrangements for deployment and control accord closely with the principle by which the ancient ruler of Yu separated and banished the Miao northward. Recently, restraints slackened somewhat, resulting in turmoil. We must once again make suitable arrangements and win their allegiance. This is a policy that cannot be altered.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school: Who among the tribal settlements is not a subject of the emperor? With imperial majesty above them, who dares harbor ambitions beyond his station? It is simply that the laws have deteriorated and people treat them lightly; another thorough rectification is needed. This essay’s planning is precise and detailed, fully displaying a grasp of statecraft.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor in a county Confucian school: It discusses affairs on the basis of facts and forms an elegantly composed essay.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school: All its proposals can be put into practice.

There are three principles for governing the non-Han peoples: benevolence, authority, and trustworthiness. Benevolence enables them to live alongside others; authority secures their nonrebellion; trustworthiness is what makes benevolence and authority effective. If one pacifies them through benevolence and awes them through authority, yet fails to win their confidence through trustworthiness, they will treat benevolence with contempt and authority with disrespect. When benevolence is treated with contempt and cannot pacify them, a warlike disposition arises; when authority is disrespected and cannot awe them, military strength is undermined. To call this skillful government of the non-Han peoples would be wrong.

The non-Han peoples of the southwest comprise many different groups. Those living between Sichuan, Huguang, and Guizhu were anciently called the Wuling Man. Some say they are descendants of the Sanmiao; others, that they are the surviving descendants of Panhu. No one knows their origins. At home, they surround themselves with bamboo thickets as defensive enclosures and obtain their food through slash-and-burn cultivation…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
出則躡枅犯險以為能執鎗衛弩前却不
常以為戰故善鬭而不畏死其性然也地
瘠而藝薄生聚既蕃則不得不鹵掠以圖
活其勢然也彼恃其善鬭而迫於圖活苟
非吾有以遏絕之則四出而無忌矣故不
可無治之之術焉柳子厚以為雖唐虞之
仁不能柔秦漢之勇不能威吾嘗因是而
求其說矣稽古治苗實昉於唐虞然惟唐
虞為善治也徂征振旅之後舞干來格之
===
餘竄其君而終就丕敘分北其民而不敢
為惡此萬世治苗之法而孰謂其不能柔
也至於周宣振中興之業方叔奏南征之
功蓋亦幾焉自是而後內之則疲我以事
夷外之則縱彼以猾夏守之則轉餉而難
久薄之則勞師而召侮而未有能得之者
楚武時蠻羅共敗楚師縊莫敖囚羣帥已
寖不可制矣吳起相悼南并蠻越拓洞庭
蒼梧之地而後有春申之宅焉是取地之
punctuated: 出則躡枅犯險以為能，執鎗衛弩，前却不常以為戰，故善鬭而不畏死，其性然也。地瘠而藝薄，生聚既蕃，則不得不鹵掠以圖活，其勢然也。彼恃其善鬭而迫於圖活，苟非吾有以遏絕之，則四出而無忌矣，故不可無治之之術焉。柳子厚以為，雖唐虞之仁不能柔，秦漢之勇不能威。吾嘗因是而求其說矣。稽古治苗，實昉於唐虞，然惟唐虞為善治也。徂征振旅之後，舞干來格之餘，竄其君而終就丕敘，分北其民而不敢為惡。此萬世治苗之法，而孰謂其不能柔也？至於周宣振中興之業，方叔奏南征之功，蓋亦幾焉。自是而後，內之則疲我以事夷，外之則縱彼以猾夏，守之則轉餉而難久，薄之則勞師而召侮，而未有能得之者。楚武時，蠻羅共敗楚師，縊莫敖，囚羣帥，已寖不可制矣。吳起相悼，南并蠻越，拓洞庭、蒼梧之地，而後有春申之宅焉，是取地之
translation_en:
…When they go out, they pride themselves on treading beams [?] and braving dangerous terrain. They wield spears and crossbows [?], fighting by unpredictable advances and retreats. Thus they fight well and do not fear death: this is their nature. Their land is barren and their harvests meager; once their population has multiplied, they have no choice but to plunder to sustain themselves: this follows from their circumstances. Relying on their fighting prowess and driven by the need to survive, they will sally forth in every direction without restraint unless we have some means of checking and stopping them. We therefore cannot dispense with methods for governing them.

Liu Zihou held that even the benevolence of Tang and Yu could not pacify them, nor could the martial might of Qin and Han overawe them. I have sought to understand this claim. Examining antiquity, we find that governing the Miao began with Tang and Yu, and indeed only Tang and Yu governed them well. After the expedition and the army’s return, after the shield dance brought them into submission, their ruler was banished and they were finally brought into full order; their people were separated and dispersed, and dared not do evil. This is the method for governing the Miao for all ages: who could say that they could not be pacified? Later, when King Xuan of Zhou undertook the restoration of his dynasty and Fang Shu achieved success in the southern expedition, they too came close to this achievement.

Thereafter, incorporating them exhausted us through attending to the Yi; excluding them gave them free rein to disturb the Chinese realm. Holding their territory required transporting provisions and was difficult to sustain; attacking them exhausted our armies and invited contempt. No one succeeded in finding the right approach. In the time of King Wu of Chu, the Man and Luo jointly defeated the Chu army; the Mo’ao hanged himself, and the commanders were imprisoned. Already they were gradually becoming impossible to control. When Wu Qi served as chief minister to King Dao, he annexed the lands of the Man and Yue to the south, extending the realm into Dongting and Cangwu; later, Lord Chunshen had his seat there. This was the beginning of the acquisition of territory…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
始也秦於是置郡黔中焉漢於是改郡武
陵焉開牂牁越巂焉唐於是分巫敘諸州
焉宋於是置都誓州及誓下州刺史焉是
皆以中國之治治之也而其不可治者卒
亦不能治若夫諸臣經略代有之矣東漢
初劉尚沒於武溪馬援隕於壺頭繼之以
梁松假之以宋均而後乃能服之雖謂之
秦漢之勇不能威可也石晉時馬希範討
溪州之叛而立銅柱以為表李弘臯銘之
===
===
趙宋時率逢原擊誠州之亂而築臺以受
降李誦記之此其最著也然特張功示伐
耳而未有能建久安長治之策者我
太祖高皇帝混一寰宇桂海氷天率被聲敎雕
題文身皆襲冠裳而况川湖之地密邇神
州首霑
聖澤非若古之處要荒之遠者乎故其設置控
馭之方於今為詳而視古為得體於湖之
永順保靖川之酉陽為之宣慰宣撫而以
punctuated:
始也。秦於是置郡黔中焉，漢於是改郡武陵焉，開牂牁、越巂焉，唐於是分巫、敘諸州焉，宋於是置都誓州及誓下州刺史焉。是皆以中國之治治之也，而其不可治者，卒亦不能治。若夫諸臣經略，代有之矣。東漢初，劉尚沒於武溪，馬援隕於壺頭，繼之以梁松，假之以宋均，而後乃能服之。雖謂之秦漢之勇不能威，可也。石晉時，馬希範討溪州之叛，而立銅柱以為表，李弘臯銘之。趙宋時，率逢原擊誠州之亂，而築臺以受降，李誦記之。此其最著也。然特張功示伐耳，而未有能建久安長治之策者。
我太祖高皇帝混一寰宇，桂海氷天，率被聲敎；雕題文身，皆襲冠裳。而况川湖之地，密邇神州，首霑聖澤，非若古之處要荒之遠者乎？故其設置控馭之方，於今為詳，而視古為得體。於湖之永順、保靖，川之酉陽，為之宣慰、宣撫，而以
translation_en:
…the beginning of the acquisition of this territory. The Qin then established Qianzhong Commandery there; the Han changed it to Wuling Commandery and opened up Zangke and Yuexi; the Tang divided it into Wu, Xu, and other prefectures; and the Song appointed prefects for Dushi Prefecture and Shixia Prefecture [?]. All these dynasties governed the region through the institutions of the Central Kingdom, yet those who could not be governed ultimately remained beyond their control. As for officials who undertook its strategic management, every age had them. Early in the Eastern Han, Liu Shang perished at Wuxi and Ma Yuan died at Hutou. Only after Liang Song succeeded them and Song Jun’s assistance was enlisted could the inhabitants be subdued. It would thus be fair to say that even the valor of Qin and Han could not overawe them. Under the Shi house’s Jin dynasty, Ma Xifan suppressed the rebellion in Xizhou and erected a bronze pillar as a marker; Li Honggao composed its inscription. Under the Zhao house’s Song dynasty, Shuai Fengyuan [?] attacked the rebels in Chengzhou and built a terrace to receive their surrender; Li Song wrote an account of it. These were the most conspicuous achievements. Yet they merely displayed accomplishments and proclaimed military merits; none devised a policy that could establish lasting peace and enduring order.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao united all under Heaven. From the southern seas of Guangxi to the frozen northern skies, all received his civilizing influence; those with tattooed foreheads and bodies all adopted caps and robes. How much more was this true of Sichuan and Huguang, so close to the heartland and among the first to receive his sagely beneficence—were they not unlike the remote outer domains of antiquity? Thus the arrangements for administration and control are now more comprehensive and, compared with those of antiquity, more fitting. In Yongshun and Baojing in Huguang, and Youyang in Sichuan, he established Pacification and Pacification Superintendency offices, and appointed…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宋誓州之後長之代有其地而留後焉
錫之誥命勉其忠義而寛其文法所以永奠諸
蠻也又為之長官司及軍民千戶所以比
次而分隸之若川之平茶貴之平頭湖之
五寨鎭溪筸子坪是也乃復以衛所環列
於外屯官軍而扼其勢洊設守備參戎假
之權而謹其防又為之總戎自督府出授
鉞開府以制其命而又有撫按以綱之藩
臬以紀之郡邑以維之
===
皇風神氣赫然而不可狎則夫裔夷聾服華夏
奠安有由也我
皇上應圖受
命敷文章化二十二年于玆矣跂行喙息莫不
竝育丕順以無失所而胡敢有弄兵以為
厲者況江漢之墟即今豐鎬而五溪在邦
域之中乎屬者蠟爾山苗聚黨成寇攻圍
疆邑焚掠保聚乃至紛兩省之軍謀煩
九重之廟議用起重臣
punctuated:
宋誓州之後長之，代有其地而留後焉。錫之誥命，勉其忠義，而寛其文法，所以永奠諸蠻也。又為之長官司及軍民千戶，所以比次而分隸之，若川之平茶、貴之平頭、湖之五寨、鎭溪、筸子坪是也。乃復以衛所環列於外，屯官軍而扼其勢，洊設守備、參戎，假之權而謹其防。又為之總戎，自督府出，授鉞開府，以制其命。而又有撫按以綱之，藩臬以紀之，郡邑以維之。皇風神氣，赫然而不可狎，則夫裔夷聾服、華夏奠安有由也。
我皇上應圖受命，敷文章化，二十二年于玆矣。跂行喙息，莫不竝育，丕順以無失所，而胡敢有弄兵以為厲者？況江漢之墟，即今豐鎬，而五溪在邦域之中乎？屬者蠟爾山苗聚黨成寇，攻圍疆邑，焚掠保聚，乃至紛兩省之軍謀，煩九重之廟議，用起重臣。
translation_en:
…the descendants of Song Shizhou [?] were appointed to govern them, holding their territories generation after generation and leaving successors. They were granted patents of appointment, encouraged in loyalty and righteousness, and treated leniently under the formal requirements of the law: these were measures to secure lasting peace among the various Man peoples. Native Chief Offices and military-and-civilian battalion commanders were also established to arrange them in ranks and apportion their subordinate jurisdictions. Examples include Pingcha in Sichuan, Pingtou in Guizhou, and Wuzhai, Zhenxi, and Ganziping in Huguang. Guards and battalions were then arrayed around their outer perimeter, with government troops stationed there to contain their power. Successive appointments of commandants and assistant regional commanders were made, investing them with authority and ensuring vigilant defense. A regional commander was also appointed over them, drawn from the Chief Military Commission and granted the ceremonial axe of command and authority to establish a headquarters, so as to control their fate. Above these, grand coordinators and regional inspectors provided overarching supervision, provincial administration and surveillance commissions maintained order, and prefectures and counties sustained the structure. Imperial influence and numinous majesty shone forth, allowing no disrespect. Thus there were sound grounds for the submission [?] of the distant Yi peoples and the settled peace of the Chinese realm.
Our Emperor has fulfilled the auspicious signs and received Heaven’s mandate, spreading civil refinement and transformation for twenty-two years now. All creatures that crawl or breathe have been nurtured together, fully obedient and each secure in its proper place. How, then, could any dare to take up arms and cause harm? All the more so when the Jiang–Han region is the Feng and Hao of our day, and Wuxi lies within the realm’s borders! Recently, the Miao of La’ershan formed bands and became raiders, attacking and besieging frontier towns and burning and plundering fortified settlements. Matters reached the point of throwing the military planning of two provinces into confusion and troubling the deliberations of the imperial court, so that a senior minister was called into service …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
錫之璽書假便宜而經略之夫苗曷為者也吾
又嘗於是而求其故矣永保酉陽與諸司
吾之所優假以控諸苗者也蓋昔者常有
師旅之役於他方則必徵兵於永保諸司
而諸司又必借助於諸苗是諸苗以其諸
司之借助也則亦無所畏於諸司而諸司
亦以其嘗借助於諸苗也則亦不欲盡去
乎諸苗是交賜而兩利焉也又况永保酉
陽相尋于仇而諸苗又挾之以規利苗無
===
敢犯永順保靖賂而永順北矣苗無敢犯
酉陽永順賂而酉陽殘矣故諸司鼎峙而
苗無不得志於其中以諸司之相為仇也
兹驅諸司而治之其德苗者固陰為之地
而其仇苗者復觀望而不為之力機失於
相疑謀敗於相忌急之則功以詭成緩之
則賊以縱逸其以老吾師而利吾之餉賞
蓋非其至謀也加以兩省偏裨勢不相攝
輕則攘功以肆侮重則推敵以賈禍或壽
punctuated: 錫之璽書，假便宜而經略之。夫苗曷為者也？吾又嘗於是而求其故矣。永保、酉陽與諸司，吾之所優假以控諸苗者也。蓋昔者常有師旅之役於他方，則必徵兵於永保諸司，而諸司又必借助於諸苗。是諸苗以其諸司之借助也，則亦無所畏於諸司；而諸司亦以其嘗借助於諸苗也，則亦不欲盡去乎諸苗。是交賜而兩利焉也。又况永保、酉陽相尋于仇，而諸苗又挾之以規利。苗無敢犯永順，保靖賂而永順北矣；苗無敢犯酉陽，永順賂而酉陽殘矣。故諸司鼎峙，而苗無不得志於其中，以諸司之相為仇也。兹驅諸司而治之，其德苗者固陰為之地，而其仇苗者復觀望而不為之力。機失於相疑，謀敗於相忌。急之則功以詭成，緩之則賊以縱逸。其以老吾師而利吾之餉賞，蓋非其至謀也。加以兩省偏裨，勢不相攝，輕則攘功以肆侮，重則推敵以賈禍，或壽
translation_en: …bestowing upon him a rescript bearing the imperial seal and granting him discretionary authority to manage the campaign. What, then, are these Miao doing? I have also sought the causes of this situation. Yongshun and Baojing, here called Yong-Bao, together with Youyang and the other native offices, are those to which we have extended favorable treatment and latitude in order to control the various Miao groups. In the past, whenever military operations arose elsewhere, troops were invariably levied from Yong-Bao and the other native offices; these offices, in turn, invariably sought assistance from the Miao. Because the offices relied on their assistance, the Miao had no fear of them. And because the offices had relied on Miao assistance, they were unwilling to eliminate the Miao entirely. Thus they conferred benefits on one another, to their mutual advantage. Moreover, Yong-Bao and Youyang pursued successive feuds, and the Miao exploited these to seek advantage. The Miao did not dare attack Yongshun, but Baojing bribed them, and Yongshun was defeated. The Miao did not dare attack Youyang, but Yongshun bribed them, and Youyang was ravaged. Thus the native offices stood opposed like the three legs of a tripod, and the Miao could achieve their aims among them precisely because the offices were enemies of one another. Now, when these offices are compelled to subdue the Miao, those grateful to the Miao secretly make room for them to maneuver, while those hostile to the Miao watch and wait, exerting no effort against them. Opportunities are lost through mutual suspicion, and plans fail through mutual jealousy. Press them hard, and achievements are fraudulently contrived; relax the pressure, and the rebels are allowed to escape. They wear out our troops and profit from our military provisions and rewards; presumably this is not their ultimate design [?]. Furthermore, the subordinate commanders of the two provinces lack authority over one another. In lesser cases, they steal credit and freely insult one another; in more serious cases, they push the enemy onto others and thereby invite disaster. Some prolong [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
張為幻以煽其習或交私市利以導其為
則今日之事其由來遠矣然則治之奈何
昔宋初有云威已立然後可議招來與之
盟則固許之臣則久方今督府決策羣工
協心提重兵壓境而奪之氣責諸司之負
國養寇而破其情則苗之亡無日矣治其
魁而威行撫其黨而恩行宣
九重之德意以示之而信行又何小醜之足慮
也執事舉以策士吾知慮不在苗之平而
===
在苗之守矣請略籌之昔韓愈有云處理
得宜自然永無侵叛之事蓋聞宣德間一
平叛苗矣于時設立灣溪等十堡而防禦
有方正德間再平反苗矣于時設立鎮筸
守備而遏絕有要初是守備之
勑也控制永保未幾有惡其害已者而去之矣
說者謂宜復之俾相攝而聯絡之可也或
相苗夷出入之喉咽鎮之以重兵又必使
湖貴之勢不分遠近之聲易達屯戍之卒
punctuated:
張為幻以煽其習，或交私市利以導其為，則今日之事，其由來遠矣。然則治之奈何？昔宋初有云：「威已立，然後可議招來。與之盟則固，許之臣則久。」方今督府決策，羣工協心，提重兵壓境而奪之氣，責諸司之負國養寇而破其情，則苗之亡無日矣。治其魁而威行，撫其黨而恩行，宣九重之德意以示之而信行，又何小醜之足慮也？執事舉以策士，吾知慮不在苗之平，而在苗之守矣。請略籌之。
昔韓愈有云：「處理得宜，自然永無侵叛之事。」蓋聞宣德間，一平叛苗矣，于時設立灣溪等十堡，而防禦有方；正德間，再平反苗矣，于時設立鎮筸守備，而遏絕有要。初是守備之勑也，控制永保，未幾有惡其害已者而去之矣。說者謂宜復之，俾相攝而聯絡之，可也。或相苗夷出入之喉咽，鎮之以重兵，又必使湖貴之勢不分，遠近之聲易達，屯戍之卒
translation_en:
…spread deceptions to inflame their habitual ways [?], or cultivate private ties and trade for profit, encouraging their conduct. Thus the present situation has origins reaching far back. How, then, should it be addressed? In the early Song, it was said: “Only after authority has been established can one discuss bringing them into allegiance. A covenant with them will make the settlement secure; allowing them to become subjects will make it lasting.” Now, if the governor’s headquarters decides upon a course and all officials act in concert, bringing a large army to bear upon the frontier to break their spirit, and calling the native chieftaincies to account for betraying the state and harboring bandits, thereby exposing their true intentions, the Miao will soon be defeated. Punish their ringleaders, and authority will prevail; pacify their followers, and benevolence will prevail; proclaim the Emperor’s benevolent intentions to them, and trust will prevail. What cause would these petty villains then give for concern? You have raised this matter as a policy question for examination candidates. I know that your concern lies not in subduing the Miao but in maintaining control over them afterward. Allow me to offer a brief consideration.
Han Yu once said: “If matters are handled appropriately, there will naturally never again be incursions or rebellions.” I have heard that rebellious Miao were subdued once during the Xuande reign. At that time, ten forts, including Wanxi, were established, providing an effective system of defense. Rebellious Miao were subdued again during the Zhengde reign. At that time, a garrison commander was appointed at Zhengan, securing a strategic means of checking them. The original imperial order for this commander charged him with controlling Yongshun and Baojing. Before long, however, some who resented the harm this did to their own interests [?] had the post abolished. Some argue that it should be restored so that the jurisdictions can exercise mutual oversight and maintain coordination. This would be acceptable. Alternatively, one could survey the strategic passageways through which the Miao tribes enter and leave, and hold them with substantial forces. It would also be essential to ensure that the forces of Huguang and Guizhou are not divided, that communications pass readily between distant and nearby places, and that the garrison soldiers…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
弗怨轉輸之計無阻可也或如宋人之法
選土豪爲苗所信服者爲總首以任彈壓
之責借補名目以榮其身而坐制之苗之
弗靖則於總首焉是責亦可也或如宋人
之法籍邊民之可用者立之團長副苗犯
一團則諸團鳴鼓應之又使諸苗之從化
者亦視民團結而策應焉又置博易場以
通其米鹽犒團長副以謹其約束亦可也
彼旣不吾擾則吾亦不彼求使彼得安耕
===
植以漸歸吾化則已矣此固有虞分北之
遺意也布置周密則疆圉鎮定彼將畏吾
威而弗敢肆示之以相保以生而非吾欲
殺之也彼將懷吾恩而弗敢忘曠然納之
包荒而坦然示之好惡彼將服吾信而弗
敢貳夫孔明之服南人服其心而已矣今
之控馭以善其後或不外此是在執事者
熟慮而徐畫之耳抑虞之格苗固惟以文
德之敷焉耳而傳復以爲究諭敎焉則聖
punctuated:
弗怨，轉輸之計無阻，可也。或如宋人之法，選土豪爲苗所信服者爲總首，以任彈壓之責，借補名目以榮其身，而坐制之。苗之弗靖，則於總首焉是責，亦可也。或如宋人之法，籍邊民之可用者，立之團長副。苗犯一團，則諸團鳴鼓應之；又使諸苗之從化者，亦視民團結而策應焉。又置博易場，以通其米鹽；犒團長副，以謹其約束，亦可也。彼旣不吾擾，則吾亦不彼求，使彼得安耕植，以漸歸吾化，則已矣。
此固有虞分北之遺意也。布置周密，則疆圉鎮定，彼將畏吾威而弗敢肆。示之以相保以生，而非吾欲殺之也，彼將懷吾恩而弗敢忘。曠然納之包荒，而坦然示之好惡，彼將服吾信而弗敢貳。夫孔明之服南人，服其心而已矣。今之控馭，以善其後，或不外此，是在執事者熟慮而徐畫之耳。抑虞之格苗，固惟以文德之敷焉耳，而傳復以爲究諭敎焉，則聖
translation_en:
…so that the garrison soldiers do not resent their service and arrangements for transporting supplies encounter no obstruction: this would be acceptable. Alternatively, following the methods of the Song, local strongmen whom the Miao trust and obey could be selected as headmen and charged with keeping order. Conferring provisional official appointments would honor them and enable us to exercise control with little effort. If the Miao failed to remain peaceful, these headmen would be held responsible. This too would be acceptable. Or, following another Song method, suitable frontier inhabitants could be registered and commanders and deputies appointed over their militia units. If the Miao attacked one unit, all the other units would beat their drums and come to its aid. Those Miao who had accepted our civilizing influence could likewise be organized into units on the model of the civilian militia and provide coordinated support. Trading grounds could also be established to facilitate their access to rice and salt, and rewards given to the militia commanders and deputies to ensure that they strictly maintained discipline. This too would be acceptable. Once they cease troubling us, we should likewise make no demands upon them. It would suffice to let them farm in peace and gradually come under our civilizing influence.
This indeed preserves the intent of the ruler of Yu’s policy of separating and dispersing the Miao. If arrangements are thorough, the frontier will be secure, and they will fear our might and dare not act recklessly. Show them that the purpose is to protect one another and sustain life, and that we do not wish to kill them; they will cherish our kindness and dare not forget it. Receive them magnanimously, embracing even the uncultivated, and plainly show them what we approve and disapprove; they will submit to our good faith and dare not waver in allegiance. When Kongming won the submission of the southerners, he did so simply by winning their hearts. Our present efforts to control them and secure a favorable lasting settlement may require nothing beyond this. It rests with those responsible to consider the matter carefully and work out their plans deliberately. Yet Yu’s bringing the Miao to submission depended solely upon spreading civil virtue. The commentary further holds that he thoroughly instructed and admonished them. Thus the sage…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人之於苗非故付之以不治者顧不以先
吾内治耳故太保之訓必先慎德祭公之
諫無取勤民而周宣之威嚴實順治以爲
之本此固制御之上策聖哲之令圖也然
則格苗威蠻以上繼虞周之烈幸有
明天子在上
punctuated: 人之於苗，非故付之以不治者，顧不以先吾内治耳。故太保之訓必先慎德，祭公之諫無取勤民，而周宣之威嚴，實順治以爲之本。此固制御之上策，聖哲之令圖也。然則格苗威蠻，以上繼虞周之烈，幸有明天子在上。
translation_en: …in dealing with the Miao, the sage did not deliberately leave them ungoverned; he simply did not give this precedence over putting our own internal affairs in order. Thus the Grand Guardian’s admonition necessarily placed careful cultivation of virtue first, and Duke Ji’s remonstrance rejected overburdening the people. Even the awe-inspiring authority of King Xuan of Zhou rested fundamentally upon orderly governance. This is indeed the highest strategy for keeping them under control, the excellent design of sages and wise rulers. To bring the Miao to submission and overawe the Man, thereby carrying forward the achievements of Yu and Zhou, we fortunately have an enlightened Son of Heaven reigning above.

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
上之二十二年癸卯維楚循彝典
闢賢科遵成
命廣舊額監察御史桂榮寔綱維
之品式條貫益恪而虔旣甄
士錄文以
獻而國奎當綴一言末簡國奎謹
===
按夏書荆州之貢杶榦栝柏
楚材之良且繁也從來遠矣
周官山虞林衡各有厲禁故
雨露之滋歲月之畜罔弗豐
楙以需世用比者
聖皇聿新
廟寢掄材之使首及荆楚復
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
上之二十二年癸卯，維楚循彝典，闢賢科，遵成命，廣舊額。監察御史桂榮寔綱維之，品式條貫益恪而虔。旣甄士、錄文以獻，而國奎當綴一言末簡。國奎謹按《夏書》，荆州之貢：杶榦栝柏。楚材之良且繁也，從來遠矣。《周官》山虞、林衡各有厲禁，故雨露之滋、歲月之畜，罔弗豐楙，以需世用。比者，聖皇聿新廟寢，掄材之使首及荆楚，復
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the twenty-second year of His Majesty’s reign, the guimao year [1543], Chu followed the established statutes and held the examination to select worthy men. In obedience to the promulgated command, the former quota was enlarged. Investigating Censor Gui Rong oversaw its conduct, ensuring still greater care and diligence in observing its standards, procedures, and regulations. Once the candidates had been selected and their essays recorded for presentation to the throne, it fell to me, Guokui, to append a few words to the closing pages.

I, Guokui, respectfully observe that the Book of Xia lists among Jingzhou’s tribute chun trees, wood for bow staves, junipers, and cypresses. The excellence and abundance of Chu’s timber thus have a long history. In the Offices of Zhou, the Mountain Foresters and Forest Wardens each enforced strict prohibitions. Thus, nourished by rain and dew and nurtured over the years, the trees all grew luxuriantly, awaiting use in the world. Recently, when our sagely emperor undertook the renovation of the ancestral temple and its chambers, the envoys charged with selecting timber went first to Jing and Chu, and again …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
遣大臣董治凡深林窈谷之產
蠻嶨夷峒之氓皆奔走牽輓
浮江達河纚纚而至而大比
之科適與期會國奎私竊有
感焉夫掄材之與遴才一也
楚之人士其沾溉培植奚翅
于木而敷榮滋息蒐剔斷斲
===
抑有甚于掄材者焉然賢才
氣運相為隆替雖木亦然昔
者文王作豐武王作鎬未聞
乏材而造德之士徵諸菁莪
棫樸之篇周召畢榮篤棐保
乂施于奕世其曰思皇多士
生此王國王國克生維周之
punctuated:
遣大臣董治，凡深林窈谷之產、蠻嶨夷峒之氓，皆奔走牽輓，浮江達河，纚纚而至。而大比之科適與期會，國奎私竊有感焉。夫掄材之與遴才一也。楚之人士，其沾溉培植奚翅于木，而敷榮滋息、蒐剔斷斲，抑有甚于掄材者焉。然賢才、氣運相為隆替，雖木亦然。
昔者文王作豐，武王作鎬，未聞乏材。而造德之士，徵諸《菁莪》《棫樸》之篇，周、召、畢、榮篤棐保乂，施于奕世。其曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之
translation_en:
…dispatched high ministers to oversee the work. The products of deep forests and secluded valleys, and the people of the Man mountain settlements [?] and Yi grottoes, all came in an unbroken succession: the people hurried to haul the timber, floating it along the Yangzi and onward to the Yellow River. The triennial Provincial Examination happened to coincide with this undertaking, and I, Guokui, was privately moved to reflect upon it. Selecting timber and selecting talent are one and the same.
