How much greater than the watering and cultivation of trees has been the nurture bestowed upon the scholars of Chu! Their flourishing and growth, their selection and pruning, their cutting and shaping, indeed involve more than the selection of timber. Yet worthy talent and the fortunes of the age rise and decline together; even timber is subject to this.
In former times, King Wen built Feng and King Wu built Hao, and we hear of no shortage of timber. As for men of cultivated virtue, evidence may be found in the poems “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) and “The Oak and the Shrub” (Yu pu). The lords of Zhou, Shao, Bi, and Rong devoted themselves to assisting, protecting, and governing, their influence extending through successive generations. As the poem says: “Ah, the many illustrious men, born in this royal kingdom! The kingdom can bring them forth; they are Zhou’s…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
楨楨也者擬諸其材也其後
依日月乗風雲若豐沛故人
南陽貴族凌煙舊臣陳橋宿
將率多椎魯頑鈍文辭佻薄
之人其可稱引者張留侯鄧
高密魏鄭公趙韓王四三人
爾而出處注措之間巳不免
===
君子之訾議譬彼木焉其適
用也淺矣則才豈易得者哉
維
聖天子
應曆協圖
握符受錄江漢之間比于豐鎬
非漢唐宋四君所彷佛也精
punctuated:
楨。」楨也者，擬諸其材也。其後依日月、乗風雲，若豐沛故人、南陽貴族、凌煙舊臣、陳橋宿將，率多椎魯頑鈍、文辭佻薄之人。其可稱引者，張留侯、鄧高密、魏鄭公、趙韓王四三人爾，而出處注措之間，巳不免君子之訾議。譬彼木焉，其適用也淺矣，則才豈易得者哉！
維聖天子，應曆協圖，握符受錄，江漢之間比于豐鎬，非漢唐宋四君所彷佛也。精
translation_en:
…support.” To call them “supports” is to liken them to timber. In later times, men attached themselves to the sun and moon and rode the winds and clouds of opportunity: the old companions from Feng and Pei, the noble families of Nanyang, the former ministers commemorated at Lingyan, and the veteran commanders of Chenqiao. Most were uncouth and obtuse, or frivolous and shallow in their literary expression. Those worthy of citation amounted to only three or four: Zhang Liang, Marquis of Liu; Deng Yu, Marquis of Gaomi; Wei Zheng, Duke of Zheng; and Zhao Pu, Prince of Han. Yet even their decisions to serve or withdraw, and their conduct in office, could not escape the criticism of gentlemen. Compared to timber, their usefulness was limited. How, then, could men of talent be easy to obtain?
Our sage Son of Heaven has answered the destined succession and accorded with the prophetic charts, grasped the tally and received the register of Heaven’s mandate. The region between the Jiang and Han rivers now compares with Feng and Hao; the four rulers of Han, Tang, and Song could not approach this achievement. The numinous essence …

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
靈之氣久畜而孕昌熙之運
濬發而會故百嘉鬯遂萬物
訢和士生其地始于感奮切
于觀摩極于漸漬故皆峩峩
濟濟接迹周士子房而下非
其儔匹雖我
皇上旁招俊乂不比近昵而帝臣
===
之共則楚之才亦莫良且繁
也國奎日事披校其毓也遠
故其辭淵以懿穆以貞其化
也久故其辭惠以莊明以粹
其遭也奇故其辭雄以紓弘
以達蓋裒然盛矣彼崇山複
嶺干霄翳日之榦苟得其一
punctuated:
靈之氣久畜而孕，昌熙之運濬發而會，故百嘉鬯遂，萬物訢和。士生其地，始于感奮，切于觀摩，極于漸漬，故皆峩峩濟濟，接迹周士，子房而下非其儔匹。雖我皇上旁招俊乂，不比近昵，而帝臣之共，則楚之才亦莫良且繁也。
國奎日事披校，其毓也遠，故其辭淵以懿，穆以貞；其化也久，故其辭惠以莊，明以粹；其遭也奇，故其辭雄以紓，弘以達。蓋裒然盛矣！彼崇山複嶺，干霄翳日之榦，苟得其一
translation_en:
…numinous vital force, long accumulated, brings forth its fruit; the fortune of flourishing prosperity wells up and converges here. Thus all good things flourish freely, and the myriad beings rejoice in harmony. Scholars born in this land begin by being stirred to aspiration, apply themselves earnestly to observing and learning from one another, and ultimately become steeped in its transforming influence. Thus they are all dignified and accomplished, following in the footsteps of the scholars of Zhou; Zifang and those below him are no match for them. Although our Emperor recruits outstanding men from far and wide, showing no partiality to those close to him, among those who serve as imperial ministers, none surpass the talents of Chu in excellence and number.
I, Guokui, daily read and assess their writings. Their cultivation has deep roots; hence their language is profound and fine, serene and upright. Their transformation has been long in the making; hence their language is gracious and dignified, lucid and pure. The circumstances they have encountered are extraordinary; hence their language is vigorous and expansive, broad and fluent. Truly, here is a magnificent abundance! Of those great trunks on lofty mountains and successive ridges, reaching into the heavens and shading the sun, if one could obtain even a single one…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
工師之喜也而連篇累牘交
輝互映主司者不幸甚矣乎
然國奎聞之傳曰人之有學
也猶木之有枝葉也學也者
亦敦其本而已矣故本實不
撥其末必榮棟楹榱桷胥此
焉出而况于人之學乎若迺
===
論篤而色莊靜言而庸違猶
之荏苒之木樗外蠹中擁腫
拳曲匠氏且弗之顧矣記曰
天下有道則行有枝葉爾多
士尚懋于學以行前言務期
與周之十臣競勳華而紹烈
光毋徒若四君佐命之臣寥
punctuated:
工師之喜也，而連篇累牘，交輝互映，主司者不幸甚矣乎？然國奎聞之，傳曰：「人之有學也，猶木之有枝葉也。」學也者，亦敦其本而已矣。故本實不撥，其末必榮，棟楹榱桷胥此焉出，而况于人之學乎？若迺論篤而色莊，靜言而庸違，猶之荏苒之木，樗外蠹中，擁腫拳曲，匠氏且弗之顧矣。

記曰：「天下有道，則行有枝葉。」爾多士尚懋于學，以行前言，務期與周之十臣競勳華而紹烈光，毋徒若四君佐命之臣寥
translation_en:
…would delight a master craftsman. Yet here, successive compositions and accumulated pages illuminate and reflect one another: is not the official presiding over the examination exceedingly fortunate? Nevertheless, I, Guokui, have heard this saying in a commentary: “A person’s learning is like a tree’s branches and leaves.” Learning, too, consists simply in strengthening the root. Thus, when the root is sound and not uprooted, its extremities will surely flourish; ridgepoles, pillars, and rafters all come from this. How much more does this apply to human learning? As for those whose discourse is earnest and whose countenance is solemn, but whose fine words are contradicted by their conduct, they resemble weak timber, ailanthus-like outside [?] and worm-eaten within, swollen, gnarled, and twisted: a craftsman would not even glance at it.

The Record of Rites says: “When the Way prevails throughout the realm, conduct has branches and leaves.” You assembled scholars should strive diligently in learning, putting the foregoing words into practice. Make it your aim to rival the splendid achievements of Zhou’s ten ministers and carry forward their glorious accomplishments. Do not merely resemble the ministers who assisted the four rulers in receiving the mandate, so few in number…

title: 嘉靖二十二年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
寥爾也則天下後世將席芘
焉矧有榮蔭于楚耶國奎遴
才者也敢借掄材之說告之
賓筵庶幾久要之義云
福建興化府莆田縣儒學教
諭黃國奎謹序
punctuated:
寥爾也，則天下後世將席芘焉，矧有榮蔭于楚耶？國奎遴才者也，敢借掄材之說告之賓筵，庶幾久要之義云。
福建興化府莆田縣儒學教諭黃國奎謹序。
translation_en:
…so few in number. Then the whole realm and later generations will enjoy their shelter—how much more will Chu enjoy their glory and shade! I, Guokui, am charged with selecting talented men. I venture to borrow this analogy of selecting timber and present it at the banquet for the honored guests, hoping thereby to fulfill the obligation of an enduring pledge.
Preface respectfully written by Huang Guokui, Instructor in the Confucian School of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian.
